**Page 319**

... figure, the five figures in the middle from which ones from the combination of Karṇas or flanks or corridors these assume the form of air-holes (*Mūṣikih*).

```sanskrit
एकादिषु द्विगुणितेष्विह यावदिष्टमूषाक्रमव्युपहितेष्वथ तेषु विद्यात्।
उद्दिष्टवेश्मकृतनिर्गममार्गमूषासत्काङ्कसैकयुतिनिर्मित्संख्यमोकः ।।८०।।
```

> In the redoubled ones headed by one, herein, till such time, the desired ones in point of the order of *mūṣās*, he may understand the adjustment of these as such. The house here has its counting devised by the addition of one having figures accompanied by *mūṣās* and exit doors created in a houses desired as such. **[80]**

```sanskrit
इति महाराजाधिराजश्रीभोजदेवविरचिते समराङ्गणसूत्रधारापरनाम्नि वास्तुशास्त्रे
आयव्ययनक्षत्रराशिफलतद्योगताराङ्कयोनितच्छन्दोगनिर्णयो नाम षड्विंशोऽध्यायः ॥२६॥
```
*Thus ends the Twenty-Sixth Chapter named 'Aya-Vyaya-Nakṣatra-Rāśiphala-Tadyoga-Tārāṅka-Yoni-Tacchandoga-Nirṇaya' in the Vāstuśāstra titled Samarāṅgaṇa-sūtradhāra, composed by the King of Kings, Illustrious Bhojadeva.*

---

## CHAPTER 27¹
### Sabhāṣṭakam (i.e., Eight Sabhās)²

```sanskrit
नन्दा भद्रा जया पूर्णा सभा स्याद् भाविता तथा।
दक्षा च प्रवरा तद्वद् विदुरा चाष्टमी मता ।।१।।
```
> *Nandā*, *Bhadrā*, *Jayā*, *Pūrṇā*, and the *Sabhā* named *Bhāvitā* as well; *Dakṣā* and *Pravarā* likewise, and *Vidurā* is recognized as the eighth. **[1]**

```sanskrit
चतुरश्रीकृते क्षेत्रे ततः षोढा विभाजिते।
मध्ये पदचतुष्कं स्यात् सीमालिन्दस्तु भागिकः ।।२।।
```
> In the field made square and thereafter divided into six segments, there should be a central square quarter of four padas, along with a border-lined balcony or verandah (*Alinda*) as a propitiate norm. **[2]**

```sanskrit
तद्वाद्योऽलिन्दकस्तद्वद् भवेत् प्रतिसराभिधः ।
प्राग्ग्रीवाख्यस्ततृतीयश्च बहिः क्षेत्राच्चतुर्दिशम् ।।३।।
```
> The one outside that deserves to be called an *Alinda* (porch, portico, or vestibule) named *Pratisara*, and the third one is named *Prāggrīva* (an entrance hall) on the outskirts of the field in all four directions. **[3]**

---

**Page 320**

```sanskrit
निसृष्टसौर्घ (धे) यैर्वा (?) स्यादेकस्यां वा यदा दिशि।
नन्दा भद्रा जया पूर्णा क्रमेण स्युः सभास्तदा।।४।।
```
> In a deserted house which may be in one quarter, a *Sabhā* (a common room) may be *Nandā*, *Bhadrā*, *Jayā*, *Pūrṇā* — in serial order, those may be the *Sabhās* then. **[4]**

```sanskrit
षड्भागभाजिते क्षेत्रे कर्णभित्तिं निवेशयेत्।
सभा स्याद् भाविता नाम सप्राग्ग्रीवात्र पञ्चमी ।।५॥
```
> In the field divided into six segments, one may introduce the flanked wall (*Karṇabhitti*). The *Sabhā* named *Bhāvitā* along with an entrance hall (*Prāggrīva*) is the fifth one here. **[5]**

```sanskrit
स्तम्भान् षट्त्रिंशदेतासु पञ्चस्वपि निवेशयेत्।
स्तम्भान् प्राग्ग्रीवसंबद्धान् पृथगेभ्यो विनिर्दिशेत् ।।६।।
```
> In these five (*Sabhās*), one may incorporate thirty-six pillars or columns. The pillars connected with the entrance halls (*Prāggrīva*) should be incorporated separately from these. **[6]**

```sanskrit
दक्षेति षष्ठी परितस्तृतीयालिन्दवेष्टिता।
प्रवरा सप्तमी द्वारैर्युक्तैषा परिकीर्तिता ।।७।।
```
> *Dakṣā*, the sixth one, is known as being engirt by the third porch or portico. The seventh one, *Pravarā*, is celebrated here as being adjusted with doors. **[7]**

```sanskrit
प्राग्ग्रीवद्वारसंयुक्ता विदुरेत्यष्टमी सभा।
सभानामिदमष्टानां लक्षणं समुदाहृतम्।।८।।
```
> Endowed with an entrance hall (*Prāggrīva*) and gates is the eighth, the *Vidurā Sabhā*. Thus, the definitions of these eight *Sabhās* stand exemplified here. **[8]**

```sanskrit
इत्यशनां लक्ष्म सम्यक् सभानामेतत् प्रोक्तं दिग्भवालिन्दभेदात्।
तद्वद् द्वारालिन्दसंयोगतश्च ज्ञातेऽत्र स्याद् भूभृतां स्थानयोगः ॥९॥
```
> This way, the definition of the eight *Sabhās* has been properly illustrated by way of the distinction of entrance halls and porches. In that very way, when calculated by the conjunction of porches and gates, there may be the combination for the abode or residence of a king, or a residence situated on a mountain. **[9]**

```sanskrit
इति महाराजाधिराजश्रीभोजदेवविरचिते समराङ्गणसूत्रधारापरनाम्नि वास्तुशास्त्रे
सभाष्टकं नाम सप्तविंशोऽध्यायः ।। २७।।
```
*Thus ends the Twenty-Seventh Chapter named 'Sabhāṣṭakam' (The Eight Sabhās) in the Vāstuśāstra titled Samarāङ्gaṇa-sūtradhāra, composed by the King of Kings, Illustrious Bhojadeva.*

### Footnotes
¹ This chapter is not included by Dr. D.N. Shukla in his *Samarāṅgaṇa-sūtradhāra Prathama Mālā*.
² **Sabhā** - A court chamber, an assembly hall, a council hall; the court hall, a palace for public meeting; a house for lodging and accommodating travellers; a dining hall; a common room, or a drawing room. (Monier-Williams, p. 1151).
```

# SAMARĀNGANA-SŪTRADHĀRA
### of Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva Paramāra

---

## CHAPTER 1: Mahāsamāgamana
### (The Insurgence of Mahāsamā (Pṛthivī)¹)

।। श्रीगणेशाय नमः ।।
*(Obeisance be to Gaņeśa)*

---

देवः स पातु भुवनत्रयसूत्रधारस्त्वां बालचन्द्रकलिकाङ्कितजूटकोटिः ।
एतत् समग्रमपि कारणमन्तरेण कार्य्यादसूत्रितमसूत्र्यत येन विश्वम् ।।१।।

May that god, the architect of the triad of worlds, having the tip of the crest knot marked by the digit of the New Moon, protect you, by whom, was created this entire universe not created in complete form barring aside the entire source (of creation) of an ulterior norm, (*samavāyī*, *asamāvāyi* and *nimitta*).²

---

सुखं धनानि ऋद्धिश्च सन्ततिः सर्वदा नृणाम्।
प्रियाण्येषां तु संसिद्धयै सर्वं स्याच्छुभलक्षणम्।।२।।

Riches, prosperity and progeny for men are (invariably) a (source) of comfort for men. The agreabilities (connected) with these are (meant) for thorough accomplishment. (Therefore) all may be such as having auspicious marks.

---

यच्च निन्दितलक्ष्मा (च?त्र) तदेतेषां विघातकृत्।
अतः सर्वमुपादेयं (यद्) भवेच्छुभलक्षणम्।।३।।

Whatever here stands as one having marks abominable that invariably is such as offering obstacles or harms. Therefore all that may be admirable (*Upādeya*) or acceptable³ or agreable, may be one as having auspicious marks.

---

देशः पुरं निवासश्च सभा वेश्मासनानि च।
यद्यदीदृशमन्यच्च तत्तच्छ्रेयस्करं मतम् ।।४।।

The country, the town, a residence, assembly or a court, a building and the seats whatever this way may be of such a sort, that is deemed as affording bliss.

---

वास्तुशास्त्रादृते तस्य न स्याल्लक्षणनिश्चयः।
तस्माल्लोकस्य कृपया शास्त्रमेतदुदीर्यते ।।५।।

Barring aside the science of Architecture¹ (the site of a house, building ground, site; a house, an abode, a dwelling place) of that there may not be any definite conclusion regarding the auspicious marks. Hence out of gracefulness for the populace this science is being dilated upon.

---

अथैकदा जगज्जन्महेतुमम्बुरुहासनम्।
पृथ्वी पृथुभयभ्रान्ता चकिताक्षी समाययौ।।६।।

Once, however, unto the one having seat for a lotus (i.e. Brahma), gone nervous owing to the terror of Prthu² (the king) having eyes bewildered (lit. enmarvelled) the Earth became encrouched or became shrunk down.

---

प्रणम्य प्रणतिप्रह्वनिखिलात्रिदशेश्वरम्।
सगद्गदमुवाचेति भूतधात्री पितामहम् ।।७।।

Having offered obeisance, to the Lord of gods (Tridaśas³) in entirety prostrated in obeisance, spoke out sobbingly the bearer of the beings (*bhūtas*), to Pitāmaha (i.e. Brahmā).

---

भगवन्नहमेतेन पृथुना पृथुतेजसा।
उप (ग? दु) ता त्वां शरणं प्राप्ता त्रायस्व मां ततः ।।८।।

Oh adorable one! I, having been made to flee away by this Pṛthu, of mighty (lit. vast) radiance or prowess, having sought refuge under you. You may protect me from him.

---

वदन्त्यामिति मेदिन्यामाविरासीदथो पृथुः ।
संरम्भमुक्तहृदयो ब्रह्माणं प्रणनाम च।।॥९॥

The earth supplicating this way, there appeared forth Prthu and bowed unto Brahmā having heart gone reft of exasperation.

---

जगादैनमथ स्निग्धध्वनिगम्भीरया गिरा।
कुर्वंस्तद्यानहंसानां पयोदध्वनिशङ्कितम् ।।१०।।

To this one he reported with a voice or speech pleasant and sombre, creating an apprehension of the rumble of clouds for the swans the very vehicles of that one.

---

त्वयास्मि जगतां नाथ! जगतोऽधिपतिः कृतः।
स्थापितानि च भूतानि सर्वाण्यपि वशे मम।।११।।

By you, Oh Lord of the sentient Beings or mobile beings! I have been made the overlord of the Universe and all the beings have been established as amenable to me.

---

तेष्वियं मम विश्वेश! कदाचिद् वशवर्तिनी।
समीकरोमि पाषाणजालान्यस्याः किलाधुना ।।१२।।

Amongst them, Oh Lord of the Universe (*Viśva*), sometimes acting in subservience to me (is this Earth). Therefore, now I render levelled or even the networks of stones (uneven so far).

---

व्यस्तानि धनुषा तावद् गौर्भूत्वेयं पलायिता।
दोग्धुकामोऽहमप्येनां चिरमन्वगमं महीम् ।।१३।।

And disordered as such, by the bow fled as it had having assumed the form of a cow. And desirous of milking this one even, I chased this earth for long.

---

यत्रक्वापि प्रयात्येषा तत्र मामेव पश्यति।
अपश्यन्त्यन्यतस्त्राणमदुग्धा त्वामुपस्थिता।।१४।।

And wherever, it went, there it saw me alone and not seeing on any other side a rescue, (operation) unmliked as such it presented itself to you.

---

अस्यां वर्णाश्रमस्थानविभागश्च विधास्यते ।
इयं च दुर्गमानेकक्षोणीधरकुलाकुला ।। १५ ।।

On this very one, the division of the orders of society and the stages of life shall be undertaken. And this one stands crowded over by intractable groups of many mountains.

---

विधास्येऽस्यां कथं त्वेतदिति मे शङ्कितं मनः ।
पृथुनेत्यथ विज्ञप्तो भगवानब्जसम्भवः ।। १६ ।।

How shall I organise over it this much, this way mind has gone apprehensive- this way was reported to by Prthu, the adorable lotus born one.

---

उवाच बोधयन्नेनं कृत्वा भूमिं च निर्भयाम्।
इयं मही महीपाल ! विधिवत् पालिता सती ।।१७।।

Spoke out making this understood that having rendered the earth free of terror this earth, Oh protector of the Earth (i.e. king)! having been guarded as per legal implications.

---

सस्यैरुत्पाद्य निष्पन्नैस्तव भोग्या भविष्यति।
यच्च ते स्यादभिप्रेतं स्थानादिविनिवेशनम् ।।१८।।

By the corns or agricultural produce having been made affluent, having produced, it will become fit for enjoyment for you. Whatever for you may be agreable a spot and the like an establishment.

---

तदेष त्रिदशाचार्यः सर्वसिद्धिप्रवर्तकः ।
सुतः प्रभासस्य विभोः स्वस्त्रीयश्च बृहस्पतेः ।।१९।। ¹

That same, the preceptor of the gods initiating all the accomplishments, the son of Prabhāsa, Vibhu and sister's son of Bṛhaspati.

---

विश्वाभिसायिधीः सर्वं विश्वकर्मा करिष्यति।
राजन्नसौ महेन्द्रस्य विदधावमरावतीम् ।।२०।।

The one having intellect circumambiating all, Viśvakarmā shall accomplish all that, Oh King! He, verily, built the Amaravati of Mahendra.

---

अन्या अप्यमुना रम्याः पुर्यो लोकभृतां कृताः।
त्वया क्षेत्रीकृतां मूर्त्ति दृष्ट्वा साद्रिद्रुमामसौ।।२१।।
सन्निवेशान् पुरग्रामनगराणां विधास्यति।
तद् गच्छ वत्स ! लोकानामितस्त्वं हितकाम्यया ।। २ २।।

Even other towns fascinating ones, of these bearing the lokas i.e. kings, have been built by this one. Having seen your image (i.e. face) having been organised into a field² or locality or having been occupied or taken possession of or having been levelled by you having mountains and trees (included), he will establish the unions³ or areas of puras (i.e. towns), grāmas⁴ and nagaras.⁵ Then proceed, Oh Child! for the desire of beneficence of the people, from here.

---

भयोज्झिता त्वमप्युर्वि ! पृथोः प्रियकरी भव।
काले स्मृतः स्मृतः पुण्यो राज्ञः प्रियचिकीर्षया ।।२३॥

Oh Earth! Divested of apprehension even you may assume an etiquette of doing good to Prthu having the merit of the king remembered repeatedly out of desire for rendering obligation.

---

त्वमप्युखिल्लमेवैतद् विश्वकर्म(न्)! करिष्यसि।
इत्युक्त्वा गमनमुपेयुषि प्रजेशेस्वं स्थानं क्षितिभुजि चाश्रिते मुदोर्ध्याम्।
प्रालेयावनिभृतमाजगाम खेलत्सिद्धस्त्रीपरिगतमाशु विश्वकर्मा।।२४।।

You, too, Oh Viśvakarman! shall undertake all this. Having said so the Lord of the subjects approaching i.e. yearning, for the occupation of his own place and the enjoyer of the Earth and the Earth as well taking recourse to their own spots with joy, came to the mountain of frost or snow having the circumambiation of the Siddha females sporting thereon, quite hastily Viśvakarmā.

---

इति महाराजाधिराजश्रीभोजदेवविरचिते समराङ्गणसूत्रधारापरनाम्नि वास्तुशास्त्रे महासमागमनो नाम प्रथमोऽध्यायः ।।१।।

*(Thus ends the first chapter named Mahāsamāgamana in the Vāstuśāstra text, otherwise known as Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra, composed by Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva.)*

---

### CHAPTER 2: The conversation between Viśvakarmā and his sons (Mānasa Putras)

अथ पृष्ठे हिमगिरेः शशाङ्कशुचिरोचिषि ।
सिद्धामरवधूभुक्तमणिमञ्चगुहागृहे ।।१।।

Then on the top of the Himagiri (i.e. Himālaya) having gleam pellucid like the moon, having abodes of grottoes beautiful owing to the gems enjoyed by the spouses of Siddhas and Gods.

विस्तीर्णासनमासीनं सर्वज्ञमथ संस्मृताः ।
आययुर्विश्वकर्माणं चत्वारो मानसाः सुताः ।।२।।

---

### FOOTNOTES & CRITICAL NOTES

#### Chapter 1 Footnotes (Page 1)
1. **महासमा (पृथ्वी) का आगमन** - Interpreted by Dr. Dvijendra Natha Sukla in Adhyāya I, Title page I - समराङ्गणसूत्रधार, प्रथम भाग published by Mehar Chand Lacchamanadas, New Delhi.
2. Dr. D.N. Sukla in verse I, Hindi translation. *असमवायि* separable cause, *समवायि* Inseparable cause and *निमित्त* the apparent cause — the three fallacies in Vaiśeşika Philosophy.
3. Sanskrit English Dictionary, Monier Williams (MW), p.213.

#### Chapter 1 Footnotes (Page 2)
1. Sanskrit English Dictionary, V.S. Apte, for 505 on Vāstu, also MW, p.948.
2. **Pṛthu**: Name of a king, son of Vena, son of Anga, the primeval monarch from whom the earth received the name Pṛthvĩ. VSA, p.347.
3. **Tridaśas**: A god, an immortal: The Thirty three gods.

#### Chapter 1 Footnotes (Page 4-5)
1. *सुतः प्रभासस्य विभोः स्वस्त्रीयश्च बृहस्पतेः* Verse 19 p.3 of Oriental Institute Baroda (OIBE) and p.7 Text part I Dr. D.N. Shukla ed. (DNSE). Dr. D.N. Shukla has substituted word वसु (Vasu) for Vibhu in his Hindi translation on p.6, verse 19 Adhyāya I समराङ्गणीय भवन निवेश का एक अध्ययन (प्रथम खण्ड और अनुवाद द्वितीय खण्ड)।
2. Dr. D.N. Shukla renders *क्षेत्रीकृताम्* as *समीकृता* i.e. rendered even or levelled as such MW p.1153 समीकरण - Levelling the act of making even.
3. VSA, p. 584 *सन्निवेशान्*.
4. **Pura / Kheta / Kharvaṭa**: A place containing large buildings surrounded by a ditch and extending not less than a Kośa in length 2 ft., it extended for half the distance, it is called a Kheta, if less then that a Kharvața or small market town : any smaller cluster of houses is called a grāma or a village MW, p.635.
5. **Grāma**: An inhabited place: village: hamlet MW p.373. Community: Race: Any number of men associated together: multitude: troop (of soldiers).
6. **Nagara**: Naga + ra: a town: a city *नगाः रायो यस्य तत् नगरम्* । *नगाः पर्वताः वृक्षाश्च*।
   *शैलोऽद्रिः शिखरी शिलोच्चयगिरि गोत्रोऽचलः सानुमान्। ग्रावा पर्वतभूधरधराहार्या नगाऽथोदयः। वृक्षोऽगः शिखरी च शाखी फलदावद्रिहरिदुदुमो जीर्णो दुर्विटपी कुठः क्षितिरुहः कारस्करो विष्टरः नन्द्यावर्त्तकरालिकौ तरुवसू पुलाक्यङ्घिपः सालाऽनोकहगच्छपादपनगाः रूक्षागमौ पुष्पदः।* (Abhidhāna Cintamani IV.93, IV.180). In both the instances *नग* has been taken as mountain as well as a tree.

---

### Appended Scholarly Commentary: Paradox of the Title "Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra"
There is an apparent paradox in the affinity of the title with the subject matter. The entire work deals with the Hindu Science of Architecture (Vāstuśāstra) but the title translates to *"The Architect of the Battle Field"*.

To resolve this, see the learned article by **Dr. U.N. Upadhyaya** entitled *"Skandhāvāra of Ancient Cities"* (Journal of the Ganganatha Jha, Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeeth, Allahabad, Vol. XLI, Parts 1-4, January-December 1985, pp.11-17).

**Summary of the Article:**
* In Ancient times, military camps (*Skandhāvāra*) played a prominent role in the establishment and development of cities.
* Before commencing construction of a permanent town, a site was selected to serve as a base for military operations against enemies. These strategic bases gradually grew into well-developed cities.
* Dr. Upadhyaya bases his article mainly on B.B. Datt's *Town Planning in Ancient India* (p.39), which notes that it was an almost invariable principle emphasized by the Śilpaśāstras that each new ruling dynasty should lay out its own capital. This new capital likely developed from a *Skandhāvāra* site possessing all the requisite characteristics of a planned city.
* Dr. Upadhyaya refers to Kautilya's *Arthaśāstra* (X.1.1-17, text p.233: *स्कन्धावार निवेशः* - "Establishment of the camp" / "Setting up of the camp", translated by R.P. Kangle, Part II, pp. 501-503).
* **Textual Reference from Arthaśāstra:**
  > वास्तुकप्रशस्ते वास्तुनि नायकवर्धकिमौहूर्तिकाः स्कन्धवारं, वृतं दीर्घ चतुरस्रं वा भूमिवशेन वा चतुर्दारं षट्पथं नवसंस्थानं मापयेयुः खातवप्रसाल द्वाराद्दालकसम्पन्नं भये स्थाने च।
* **Kangle's Translation Note:** As a site approved by experts in the science of building, the commandant (*nāyaka*), carpenters (*vardhaki*), and astrologers should cause the camp to be set up—circular, rectangular, or square in conformity with the nature of the ground—with four gates, six roads, and nine divisions, endowed with a moat, a rampart, a parapet, gates, and towers, when there is danger and where the army has to halt. (Note: The translation styles vary slightly across editions cited by Dr. Upadhyaya, including T. Ganapati Sastri's commentaries).
```

# SAMARĀNGANA-SŪTRADHĀRA
### of Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva Paramāra

---

## CONCLUSION OF CHAPTER 1: Mahāsamāgamana

भयोज्झिता त्वमप्युर्वि ! पृथोः प्रियकरी भव।
काले स्मृतः स्मृतः पुण्यो राज्ञः प्रियचिकीर्षया ।।२३॥

Oh Earth! Divested of apprehension even you may assume an etiquette of doing good to Prthu having the merit of the king remembered repeatedly out of desire for rendering obligation.

---

त्वमप्युखिल्लमेवैतद् विश्वकर्म(न्)! करिष्यसि।
इत्युक्त्वा गमनमुपेयुषि प्रजेशेस्वं स्थानं क्षितिभुजि चाश्रिते मुदोर्ध्याम्।
प्रालेयावनिभृतमाजगाम खेलत्सिद्धस्त्रीपरिगतमाशु विश्वकर्मा।।२४।।

You, too, Oh Viśvakarman! shall undertake all this. Having said so the Lord of the subjects approaching i.e. yearning, for the occupation of his own place and the enjoyer of the Earth and the Earth as well taking recourse to their own spots with joy, came to the mountain of frost or snow having the circumambiation of the Siddha females sporting thereon, quite hastily Viśvakarmā.

---

इति महाराजाधिराजश्रीभोजदेवविरचिते समराङ्गणसूत्रधारापरनाम्नि वास्तुशास्त्रे महासमागमनो नाम प्रथमोऽध्यायः ।।१।।

*(Thus ends the first chapter named Mahāsamāgamana in the Vāstuśāstra text, otherwise known as Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra, composed by Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva.)*

---

## CHAPTER 2: The Conversation Between Viśvakarmā and His Sons (Mānasa Putras)

अथ पृष्ठे हिमगिरेः शशाङ्कशुचिरोचिषि ।
सिद्धामरवधूभुक़्तमणिमञ्चगुहागृहे ।।१।।

Then on the top of the Himagiri (i.e. Himālaya) having gleam pellucid like the moon, having abodes of grottoes beautiful owing to the gems enjoyed by the spouses of Siddhas and Gods.

---

विस्तीर्णासनमासीनं सर्वज्ञमथ संस्मृताः ।
आययुर्विश्वकर्माणं चत्वारो मानसाः सुताः ।।२।।

In vicinity of (lit. towards Viśvakarmā) the omniscient, seated on a broad seat, came the four sons, the mind born ones.

---

जयो विजयसिद्धार्थो चतुर्थश्चापराजितः ।
तमुपागम्य शिरसा नेमुः प्राञ्जलयो मुनिम् ।।३।।

Jaya, Vijaya, Siddhārtha and Aparajita having approached the sage offered obeisance to him having hands folded.

---

तानुवाच मुनिर्वत्साः ! विदितं वो यथा पुरा।
वास्तु ब्रह्म सदा विश्वं व्याप्नोति सकलं जगत् ।।४।।

To them spoke out the sage- Oh Children! well known it is to you that earlier, the entire-mobile creation circumambiating the Universe, had perennially an architectural evolution or material cause of the visible universe or all pervading soul and spirit of the universe from which all created things are produced and into which they are absorbed.¹

---

धर्म्य कर्म तदा स्वेष्टप्राप्त्यै लोकावनानि च।
व्यवस्थाप्य चकारैष लोकपालश्च कल्पनाम्।।५।।

Then for the gain of his own cherished end, having well established the acts suited to spiritual good or piety or law and (conducive to) the protection of the populace or people or world, brought about this imaginative understanding being the Lokapāla, i.e. the guardian of the Universe.

---

अहमप्यमुना विश्वनाथेनाम्बुजजन्मना।
लोकानां सन्निवेशार्थमादिष्टोऽस्मि स्वयम्भुवा ।।६।।

Even I, by the Lord of Viśva (Universe), the one having birth from the lotus (i.e. Brahmā) for the sake of setting up the lokas (the habitations or people), have been ordained by Svayambhū the self born one.

---

रम्याणि नगरोद्यानसभास्थानान्यथो मया।
सुरासुरोरगादीनां निर्मितान्यात्मबुद्धितः।।७।।

By me, by dint of my intelligence have been built fascinating Assembly Halls, gardens and towns of gods, demons and Uragas i.e. Nāgas.

---

गत्वोर्वी वैन्यनृपतेर्वत्साः ! प्रियचिकीर्षया।
नगरग्रामखेटादीन् करिष्यामि पृथक् पृथक्।।८।।

Now having gone over to the Earth in light of the cherished end for a creation of the king Vainya (son of Vena, i.e. Prthu), shall create separately, nagaras, grāmas and khetas.¹

---

कार्ये त्वमुष्मिन् सकले मम विश्वसृजार्पिते।
सम्यक्साहायकैर्भाव्यं भवद्भिरिति नः स्थितम्।।९।।

It stands intentioned by us that by you all should be acted as adjuncts or helpers or co-ordinators quite suitably in that task in entirety devolved on me by the creator of the Universe.

---

यतस्त्रिभुवनालोकप्रोद्यतस्याब्जिनीपतेः ।
सहायतां तमश्छेदे कलयन्ति मरीचयः ।।१०।।

Because the rays of the Lord of lotuses, i.e. the sun render succour in obviation of the gloom when risen up as illuminator of the lokas i.e. the spacious spheres or the worlds, you likewise help me in this task which is meant to radiate or elevate the glory of the world.

---

स्वयं करिष्येऽहमथो निवासाय पृथोः पुरीम्।
विचित्रनगरग्रामखेटामतिमनोहराम्।।११।।

I shall create myself a city i.e. a habitat for a residence of Prthu having variety of nagaras, grāmas and Khețas and highly gorgeous or fascinating.

---

भवन्तः पुनरागत्य चत्वारोऽपि चतुर्दिशम्।
तांस्तान् निवेशान् कुर्वन्तु पृथग्जनकृताश्रयान्।।१२।।

You all then having turned up, all of you four, within the four quarters may create those habitats having shelter accorded to men of distinct statures.

---

अन्तरेष्वध्वपाथोधिशैलानां सरितां तथा।
विधातव्यानि दुर्गाणि नृपाणां भयशान्तये ।।१३।।

For the obviation of the fear of the kings between the spaces, land routes, oceans and mountains the forts deserve to be created or built.

---

वर्णप्रकृतिवेश्मानि संस्थानानि च लक्ष्मभिः।
विधेयानि प्रतिग्रामं प्रतिपूः प्रतिपत्तनम्।।१४।।

*(Text continues...)*

This mirrors Bhartṛhari’s *Vairāgya Śataka* (verse 82), explicitly indexed as Verse No. 9 under the miscellaneous/appended verses (*संकीर्ण श्लोका*) at the conclusion of the standard text edited by M.R. Kale.

#### Chapter 2 Footnotes (Page 3)
1. **Settlement Typologies:** * *खेटः पुरार्द्धविस्तरः* — A *Kheṭa* is defined as half the scale or extension of a *Pura*. It indicates a small agricultural peasant settlement or village hub (*Abhidhāna Cintāmaņi* IV.38, p.241).
   * *शाखापुरं तूपपुरं* — Satellite or secondary townships.
   * *नगरी पूः पुरीद्रङ्गः पत्तनम् पुटभेदनम्* — Typologies of cities, commercial ports, and fortified urban centers (*Abhidhāna Cintāmaņi* IV.37, p.240).
   * *निवेशनमधिष्ठानम् स्थानीयं निगमोऽपि च* — Settlements, operational bases, market towns, and headquarters.
   * *स्कन्धावारो राजधानी* — A military base/camp functioning directly as a capital city (*Abhidhāna Cintāmaņi* IV.39, p.241).

## CHAPTER 3: Praśna (A Questionnaire)

तस्मादुवाच मुनिर्वत्साः ! विदितं वो यथा पुरा...
*(Note: Transition text from Chapter 2 concluding elements)*

The abodes of castes or orders of society, the constituent elements of the state $(Prakrti)^{1}$ or subjects and the Institutes or Institutions by demarcation deserve to be created in every village, town and pattana. [cite: 394]

---

तानित्यमात्मतनयानभिधाय सम्यक् सारार्थभूतमपरिस्फुटतोज्झितं च।
स्थानार्पितोरुभरनिर्वृतचित्तवृत्तिस्तूष्णीं प्रभासतनयो नयविज्जगाम ।।१५।।

Having addressed this way gracefully to those sons, having tendency of mind thoroughly satisfied, having burden supported on the liability indistinctly attributed being of an essence grounded one, the son of Prabhāsa, a diplomat or a polity skilled one, observed silence. [cite: 397]

इति महाराजाधिराजश्रीभोजदेवविरचिते समराङ्गणसूत्रधारापरनाम्नि वास्तुशास्त्रे विश्वकर्मणः पुत्रसंवादो नाम द्वितीयोऽध्यायः ।।
*(Thus ends the second chapter named Viśvakarmaṇaḥ Putra-saṁvāda in the Vāstuśāstra text, otherwise known as Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra, composed by Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva.)* [cite: 399]

श्रुत्वा कृताञ्जलिः प्राह स्निग्धगम्भीरया गिरा।।१।।

Then among them the one named Jaya having heard that expression of Viśvakarmā, having hands folded, spoke out in a voice pleasing and sombre. [cite: 405]

वृणोषि तेन न वयमात्मानं बहु मन्महे ॥२॥

As sole quarry of learning or knowledge, the way you are choosing us by way of help (i.e. helping hands), by that we do not deem ourselves as highly esteemed² or by that we are deeming ourselves as highly honoured. [cite: 408]

अप्रमेयप्रभावस्त्वं सर्वमाख्यातुमर्हसि ।। ३ ।।

Therefore, now for the sake of well being of the subjects also of ours or descendants or progenies of ours. Aye Lord! you being one as having power of unmeasurable norm or inestimable nature, deserve to narrate all that. [cite: 419]

---

पूर्वमेकार्णवे जाते जगति प्रलयं गते।
महाभूतामरपुरीज्योतिषां कथमुद्भवः।।४।।

The Universe having gone to dissolution and an ocean of a solitary extent having ensured, how the birth of huge animals or mighty beings and the luminaries of the city of gods took genesis or how the birth of Amarapuri or the city of gods and luminaries came about. [cite: 422]

---

किमाकारा किमाधारा किंप्रमाणा च मेदिनी।
विस्तृतिः परिधिश्चास्या बाहुल्यमपि कीदृशम्।।५।।

What shaped, what plighted or what propped one or how based one, what extended one, is the Earth and what circumference (*paridhih*) and what covering area is of this one and its vastness (*bāhulya*) or plenitude is of what sort? [cite: 425]

---

उच्छ्रायव्यासदीर्घत्वैः कैः केऽस्यां कुलभूभृतः ।
कति ख्यातानि वर्षाणि द्वीपा नद्योऽब्धयस्तथा।।६।।

By height, expanse and length or by height, latitude and longitude and width or breadth (*Vyāsa*) which ones are its Hereditary mountains (*Kulabhūbhṛtaḥ*¹) or principal mountains (supposed to exist in each division of the continents). How many are known as the Varşas (divisions of the world)² and the Islands, rivers and the oceans. [cite: 428, 429]

---

काः सूर्येन्दुग्रहर्धादिगतयश्च पृथक् पृथक्।
भूमेरुपरि किं चैषामन्योन्यं प्रोक्तमन्तरम्।।७।।

What are the separate circulations of the sun, moon, planets and the constellations or signs of the zodiacs or the seven stars called the pleiades afterwards the seven Rșis and over the Earth what variation proper or distinction proper or reaction proper of these is proclaimed as such? [cite: 432]

---

किमाधारं दिवि ज्योतिश्चक्रं भ्रमयते च कः।
लोके कथं महाभूतान्यूर्ध्वाधो बिभ्रति स्थितिम् ।।८।।

What prop or fulcrum in the sky makes the circle of stars rotate and in the universe, how the mighty beings sustain the position above and below. [cite: 442]

---

युगधर्मव्यवस्थाभिः काश्चादौ लोकवृत्तयः।
कश्वादिमस्ततो राज्ञां ग्रहाणां वर्णिनां कथम्।।९।।

By the legacies of the law codes in the aeons what were in the beginning the tendencies of the people? Who then was the primeval one among the kings, the planets or comets and the varņins (the persons of the four castes)? [cite: 446, 447]

---

कति देशाः कति भुवः पृथक्त्वेन निरूपिताः ।
कार्यः क्व च कथं सन्निवेशो जनपदाश्रयः ।।१०।।

How many countries, how many lands were demarcated by way of distinction. And where is to be established the habitat of those recumbent on the Janapadas (the principalities of the people). [cite: 452, 453]

---

व्यक्तचिहैः स्वनस्पर्शगन्धवर्णरसादिभिः।
काः शस्ता निन्दिताः काश्च पुराणामपि भूमयः ।।११।।

By the apparent marks, by the colour, scent, touch and sound and the like, what appreciable and what detestable are the lands of the cities? [cite: 456, 459]

कार्यं केन विधानेन भूभृत्पुरनिवेशनम्।

किंफलं सुनिविष्टेऽस्मिन् दुर्निविष्टे च किं पुनः ।।१३।। *(Note: variants in source text line 463)* किमागप्रपुरसंस्थानमनिन्द्यं किं च निन्दितम्।।१३।।

कश्चात्रानुक्रमविधिः प्रमाणैरुपपादितः।
प्राकारगोपुराट्टालपरिखावप्रकर्म च।।१४।।

And which one modicum of organisation stands established by factual representation and what (work) regarding the (creation) of ramparts, turrets, and balconies or upper-storeyed apartments, the moats, mounds or the gates of fortified towns or ditches, has been undertaken. [cite: 466, 471]

---

तमङ्गनिर्गमद्वारप्रतोल्यट्टालकादिभिः ।
कीदृशः प्रविभागश्च रथ्याचत्वरवर्त्मभिः ।।१५।।

By the platforms¹ and exit gates the Broad ways or Principal roads through towns and villages and the upper roofs or balconies and by the routes of the sequence or quardrangles and streets or lanes or arcades, what sort of divisions stand organised. [cite: 474]

---

1. **Prakṛti / Elements of State:** *स्वाम्यमात्यजनपददुर्गकोशदण्डमित्राणि प्रकृतयः* (KAŚ I.VI.1.1). King, minister, territory, fort, treasury, army, ally. [cite: 413]
2. **Metre Note:** Dr. D.N. Shukla's edition text p.9 verse 2 is missing the syllable "na", causing an anomaly in the classical Anustubh metre structure rules (*श्लोके षष्ठं गुरुज्ञेयं...*). [cite: 414, 415]
3. **Kulaparvatas / Principal Mountains:** *महेन्द्रो मलयः सह्यः शुक्तिमानृक्षपर्वतः। विन्द्यश्च पारियात्रश्च सप्तैते कुलपर्वताः ।।* (MW p.155). [cite: 433]

5. **Kheṭaka:** Settlement inhabited by agricultural peasants (MW p.340). [cite: 486]
6. **Śakradhvaja / Indramaha Festival:** Referenced in Varāhamihira’s *Bṛhatsaṁhitā* (Ch. 43) and Bharata’s *Nāṭyaśāstra* (1.54) as celebratory flags marking state expansion or ritual initiation. [cite: 487, 510]
7. **Vayas:** Bodily or mental strength/enjoyment factor (MW p.920). [cite: 516]

9. **Niryūha:** Architectural projections over gateways or structural pillars modeled conceptually on elephant profiles or decorative pegs. [cite: 559, 562]
10. **Antarajah:** Organisms generated inside biological or material bodies (worms/moths). [cite: 566]
11. **Bhūśreṣṭha:** Elite of the ground (interpreted as Brāhmaṇas). [cite: 565]
12. **Kāla (Arts):** The traditional list of 64 modular human arts found throughout the *Kāmasūtra* and *Śukranīti*. [cite: 583]
13. **Dhiṣṇya:** Subordinate structural side altars or mounds over which baseline ritual configuration happens. [cite: 591]
14. **Plinth / Mūlapāda:** Core structural base footing of structural units (VSA p.347). [cite: 639]
15. **Sthūṇā:** Supporting column or post framework. [cite: 659]
16. **Lupā:** Architectural structural brackets, slopes or eaves (*Meharāv* profiles). [cite: 665]
17. **Mūṣā:** Structural round windows or air filtration vents. [cite: 689]

# SAMARĀNGANA-SŪTRADHĀRA
### of Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva Paramāra

---

## CHAPTER 4: Sṛṣṭi-Varṇana (The Description of Creation / Mahadādi Sarga¹)

जयस्येति समाकर्ण्य विश्वकर्मा च तद् वचः।
जगाद गर्जदम्भोदध्वनिगम्भीरया गिरा।।१।।

This way having listened to the expression as such of Jaya, Viśvakarmā exclaimed in a voice sombre like the sound of the cloud rumbling as such. [cite: 226]

---

साधु वत्स ! त्वया सम्यक् प्रज्ञयातिविशुद्धया।
प्रश्नोऽयमीरितो वास्तुविद्याब्जवनभास्करः ।।२।।

All right Oh Child! by you by intellect highly pure rightly has been put forth this question the very sun for the grove of lotuses in the form of science of architecture. [cite: 229]

---

सत्वं निधाय प्रश्नानां समुदायममुं हृदि।
वदतो मेऽवधानेन शृणु यद् ब्रह्मणोदितम्।।३।।

That (same) you having kept in mind, the volley of questions, you may listen with care while I am saying what has been spoken by Brahmā. [cite: 232]

---

इदमासीद् युगान्ताग्निप्लुष्टं संवर्तकादिभिः।
समुत्सृजद्भिरम्भांसि विश्वमेकार्णवीकृतम्।।४।।

This universe was such as having been transformed into one ocean by the cloud of dissolution or fire of destruction or submarine fire² or periodical destruction or dissolution of the world and the like, generating waters having been calcined by the fire of the end of the aeon. [cite: 235, 240]

---

तमोभूते ततस्तस्मिन् भोगिपर्यङ्कमाश्रितः।
हरिः सुष्वाप सलिले कृत्वोदरगतं जगत्।।५।।

Then that having got converted into a gloom resorted on to the couch of serpent Vişnu slept in water having rendered the mobile existence as gone into the stomach. [cite: 243, 244]

---

अथास्य नाभावम्भोजमभूत् तस्मिन्नजायत।
सर्वज्ञानाश्रयः श्रीमांश्चतुर्वक्त्रः सुरेश्वरः ।॥६॥

Then in the navel of this one a lotus sprang up. In that took (birth) the Lord of gods the four faced one, the illustrious one, the one repose of all the knowledge or sciences. [cite: 247, 248]

---

स कदाचिद् दधच्चेतः प्रजासृष्टिं प्रति प्रभुः।
महान्तमसृजतम् तत्र पूर्वं विश्वस्य हेतवे ।।७।।

That Lord, sometimes having heart composed as such, regarding the creation of progeny, created a gigantic one a being (*Mahat*), therein to begin with for the purpose of the universe. [cite: 251]

---

त्रिधाहङ्कृतमेतस्मान्मनोऽभूत् सात्त्विकादतः ।
राजсадपि चाक्षाणि तन्मात्राणि च तामसात् ।।८।।

Three times from that an egoism or *ahaṅkāra* got created and from that the *Sāttvika* one mind was born and from the *rājasa* one senses got birth and from the *tāmasa* the *tanmātrās* i.e. the subtle and primary elements such as — *śabda* (sound), *rasa* (taste), *sparśa* (touch), *rūpa* (form) and *gandha* (smell). [cite: 254]

---

तेभ्यः पञ्च महाभूतान्याविरासन्ननुक्रमात्।
व्योमादीनि धरान्तानि स्वैः स्वैर्युक्तानि तैर्गुणैः ।॥९।।

From those (elements) five gigantic beings (*Mahābhūtas*) appeared forth in serial order, starting with sky and ending with earth endowed with individual merits of their respective categories. [cite: 257]

---

अधरोत्तरभावश्च सम्यगेषामथोच्यते ।
आदौ पृथ्वी ततोऽधस्तादापस्तासां च पावकः ।।१०।।
तस्याप्यधस्तात् पवनस्ततः खमवकाशदम्।
भूतादिस्थं वियत् सोऽपि महता परिवारितः ।।११।।

The idea of their being above and below is now properly being dilated upon. To begin with the earth and below that the waters and below, these the fire. And even below that is the wind and thereafter (below) that the sky affording an open space or hemisphere. And having beings well established the sky (even exists as such). And that one even (i.e. the wind) stands enveloped by a gigantic norm. [cite: 262, 263, 267, 268, 269]

---

महांश्च विशति व्यक्तं व्यक्तमव्यक्तकं पुनः।
ग्राह्यग्राहकभावेन व्यक्तो भूतसमुद्भवः ॥१२॥

And the gigantic one enters the specific one or the distinct one and the specific one gets into the indistinct or unspecific one. By the ideology of *grāhya* and *grāhaka* (i.e. one fit to be accepted and the one who accepts or seizes), the specific one is the very provenance of beings. [cite: 272, 273]

---

आधाराधार्यभावश्च यथार्थों च स्थितिव्ययौ।
महाभूतानि सगुणान्येवं सृष्ट्वा ततः प्रभुः ॥१३।।

And the ideology of the prop and the one fit to be propped and the existence and defunction being of a signification, having created the gigantic beings, endowed with *guṇas* or merits the Lord. [cite: 276]

---

मनः पुनरसौ सर्गे भौतिके सम्यगादधौ।
सुरासुरान् सगन्धर्वान् यक्षरक्षांसि पन्नगान् ।।१४।।

Concentrated the mind once again quite evidently on the elemental creation. To the gods and demons, accompanied by the Gandharvas, the Yakşas, the Rākṣasas and the serpents (*Pannagas*). [cite: 279, 280]

---

नागान मुनीनप्सरसो मनसा समजीजनत्।
अर्केन्दू चक्षु (षी?षो) जातौ गगनभ्रमणक्षमौ।॥ १५॥

The nagas, the sages, the nymphs he created through mind. The sun and the moon took birth in the eye capable of wandering in the firmament. [cite: 283, 284]

---

गात्रेभ्योऽपि च नक्षत्रचक्रमस्मादजायत।
इन्द्रियेभ्यश्च पञ्चभ्योऽभूत् ताराग्रहपञ्चकम ।। १६ ।।

And from the limbs also the constellation of stars or group of planets and from the five senses took birth the pentad of planets and comets. [cite: 287]

---

ग्रहत्वं पुनरेतेषामिन्द्रियग्रहणाद् विदुः।
सुरेन्द्रचापचिह्नानां विद्युद्वलयशालिनाम्।।१७।।

The seizure of these having marks of Rainbow glamour with the lightning globes they understood by the seizure of the senses or by the suppression of the senses. [cite: 290]

---

भीमाशनिभृतां चासीत् केशेोध्योऽम्बुमुचां भवः ।
विश्वमापूरयन् कृत्स्नमाविरासीत् तदिच्छया ।।१८।।
त्रिलोकीपावनस्तिर्यग्गामी चण्डः समीरणः।
ततश्चण्डानिलोद्धृतमुपर्यर्मांशुतापितम् ।।१९।।
वायुभिः शोषमानीतं जगाम घनतां पयः।

Of these bearing terrific lightning, the water releasing ones i.e. clouds, the provenance came along from the curls. And inflating the universe in entirety there appeared forth by the desire of these ones, the terrific squall (*samīraṇa*) moving in a circuitous movement. Then quaked by the terrific squall heated by the solar beams above, by the breezes brought to desiccation the water assumed floridity or density. [cite: 297, 298, 299]

---

तस्योपरिष्ठादम्भोधेरधः कुण्डलितं वपुः ।।२०।।
विष्णोः सज्या (? शय्या) त्वमभ्येत्य धत्तेऽनन्तोऽखिलां भुवम्।
न तप्तं येषु येष्वम्भः प्रदेशेष्वर्करश्मिभिः ।।२१।।

From the top of that one below the ocean the body rolled down as such. Of Vişnu having attained to the state of a couch Ananta props up the entire earth and the areas proper in which the water was not heated by the solar rays. [cite: 300, 303, 304]

---

नीतं न वानिलैः शोषं तत्र तत्राब्धयोऽभवन्।
महाम्भोवीचिसङ्घाता विक्षिप्ताश्चण्डमारुतैः ।।२२।।

Nor was it brought to the state of desiccation. There and in other spots oceans developed. And the floods of the ripples or showers of billows of vast waters splashed forth by terrific hurricanes. [cite: 307, 308]

---

यत्र यत्रापुरैक्यं ते तत्र तत्राद्र्योऽभवन्।
निश्चलत्वार्थमवनिश्चर्मवद् वितताथ तैः ।।२३।।
शैलैः कीलैरिव स्थानेष्वाचिता तेषु तेष्वियम्।
वृद्धि गताद्रिनिःष्यन्दैर्भूभृतां प्रविभागजा ।। २४।।

Where ever they attained to the state of oneness, there the mountains grew up. For the sake of immobility, the earth spread like the skin or hide. And by those mountains, like nails or spikes it was rounded off in those and other spots. Attained to growth by the spread of the mountain springs sprung from the division of mountains stream got created. [cite: 312, 313, 314, 315]

---

निम्नगाभूत् ततोऽम्भोधेः कान्ता निम्नानुसारिणी।
मेदिन्यन्तेषु जलधिपर्यन्तेषु विनिर्ययुः ।॥२५॥

Then in the corners of the earth, the spouse of the ocean following the lower regions got out from out of the extremities of ocean. [cite: 316]

---

अम्भांसि यत्र यत्रासंस्ते द्वीपाश्चित्ररूपिणः ।
सनिम्नगाम्बुधिद्वीपा विभक्ताखिलभूधरा ।। २६ ।।

Where-so-ever there were waters those became Islands of varied extent and the entire earth got divided into Islands with oceans and rivers. [cite: 320, 321]

---

व्यक्ता बभूव कृत्स्नैवं भूमिभूतानि बिभ्रती।
स चक्रे रौरवादीनां निरयाणामधः क्षितेः ।।२७।।

Bearing the beings the entire earth became apparent. And He (i.e. Brahmā) created below the earth the region of Hells such as Raurava³ and the like. [cite: 324]

---

स्वकर्मफलभुक्त्यर्थं स्थानं दुष्कृतकर्मणाम्।
जरायुजाण्डजोद्भिज्जस्वेदजैः सह स प्रभुः॥२८॥

For the sake of suffering the outcome of personal failings being (the abode) of evil deeds, along with the viviparous (*Jarāyujas*⁴), oviparous (*Andajas*), germination born as plants (*Udbhijjas*) and those born from moisture (*Svedajas*). [cite: 327]

---

चतुर्धेत्यसृजल्लोके भूतग्रामं चराचरम्।
द्वेधा जरायुजास्तत्र मनुष्याः पशवस्तथा।। २९ ।।

He created in the world or universe, the classification of beings the mobile as well as immobile. The viviparous were of two kinds, the men and the animals. [cite: 328, 330]

---

ग्राम्याः सप्ताभवंस्तेषु सप्तारण्यकृतालयाः ।
पुमान् गौस्तुरगच्छागौ मेषो वेगसरः खरः ॥३०॥

Seven among them were known as those belonging to the grāmas or villages or habitats and seven having abodes for forests; viz. the man, the cow, the horse, the goat, the sheep, the mule and the donkey. [cite: 333, 334]

---

ग्रामवासैकनिरताः सप्तैते परिकीर्तिताः।
सिंहद्विपोष्ट्रमहिषाः शरभो गवयः कपिः।।३१।।
अरण्यगोचरा जीवाः सप्तैते वत्स ! निर्मिताः।

Engaged in sole habitation in the gramas or habitats, seven these stand illustrated. The lion, the elephant, the camel or dromedary, the bison or buffalo, Śarabha (the octopus), the Yak or Ox and the ape or monkey are the beings prowling along on the ground of the forests. These seven Aye! child have been created. [cite: 347, 348, 349]

---

धर्माधर्मविवेकित्वाच्छ्रेयान् ग्राम्येषु पूरुषः ।।३२।।
अरण्यचारिषु श्रेष्ठः सिंहः शौर्यबलादिभिः।

Owing to circumspection of dharma (piety) and adharma (impiety) better one is the man in the habitats. Among the forest prowlers lion is the greatest one on account of physical valour and courage. [cite: 349, 353]

---

सुपर्णा भुजगाः कीटा yeऽपि च स्युः पिपीलिकाः ।॥३३॥
चतुर्धेत्यण्डजन्मानो जन्मिनस्ते प्रकीर्त्तिताः।

The vertebrates or winged ones, the snakes, the worms and whatsoever may be the ants. The oviparous ones are of four varieties, the creatures as such they stand proclaimed. [cite: 354, 355]

---

क्लेद समुद्भूताः कृमियूकादिजन्तवः ।॥३४॥
सर्वेऽपि स्वेदजन्मानस्ते प्रजापतिना कृताः।

Those ones born from the moisture and shags: the worms and the leeches and lice and other creatures. All of them are sweat or moisture born having been created by the creator. [cite: 356, 359]

---

उद्भिज्जाः पञ्चधा भूत्वा निर्दिष्टाः स्थावराश्च ते ।। ३५॥
दुमा वल्ल्यश्च गुल्माश्च वंशाः सतृणजातयः ।

The germination ones as plants having assumed five forms have been indicated as the immobile ones: the trees, the creepers, the bushes or under-woods or stalks, the bamboos or reeds and those of the species of water breeds. [cite: 360, 363]

---

छन्नान्तःकरणत्वं च स्वस्थानात्त्यागितापि च ।।३६।।
छिन्नप्ररोहिता चैषां वैशेषिकगुणत्रयम्।
गायत्री भूतसंज्ञैषा चतुर्विंशतिपर्विका ।।३७।।

Those having the idea of inner conscience unravelled and the point of not learning the spot (of growth) having the norm of growing when pruned or lopped off or cut off, the quality triad is quite patent with them. Gayatri⁵ (the catechu plantation of trees) having the nomenclature of bhūtas is of twenty four joints. [cite: 364]

---

ज्ञात्वैनां पुरुषः पुण्यां भवति स्वर्गभाजनम्।
भुवनभूजलवह्निमरुद्वियत्प्रमुख एष भवस्तव कीर्त्तितः।
वसुमतीपरिमाणविनिश्चयं कथयतः शृणु सम्प्रति वत्स ! मे।॥३८॥

Having known this the sacred one the man becomes an object of Heaven. The universe, the earth or ground, the water, the fire, the wind and the sky or atmosphere headed by these this creativity for you has been declaimed. The extent of the earth its determination, Oh child, you may hear now, when I am talking of it. [cite: 371, 372, 373]

---

इति महाराजाधिराजश्रीभोजदेवविरचिते समराङ्गणसूत्रधारापरनाम्नि वास्तुशास्त्रेमहदादिसर्गाध्यायश्चतुर्थः।।४।।
*(Thus ends the fourth chapter named Mahadādi-Sarga in the Vāstuśāstra text, otherwise known as Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra, composed by Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva.)* [cite: 374]

---

### CHAPTER 4 FOOTNOTES
1. **Mahadādi Sarga / Sṛṣṭi-Varṇana:** Chapter IV details cosmological and physical creation systems mapped via classical Puranic and Sāṅkhya taxonomies. [cite: 236]
2. **Periodic Destruction / Dissolution:** Explored across V.S. Apte's lexicon guidelines regarding macrocosmic cyclic events. [cite: 237]
3. **The Twenty Hells:** *Manusmṛti* IV.87-90 notes explicit designations for karmic retributive zones: *Tamisra, Andhatāmisra, Mahāraurava, Raurava, Kālasūtra, Mahānaraka, Sañjīvana, Mahāvīcī, Tapana, Sampratāpana, Saṁhāta...* [cite: 338, 339, 340]
4. **Four Generational Matrices:** Viviparous (*Jarāyuja*), Oviparous (*Aṇḍaja*), Sweat-born/Moisture-born (*Svedaja*), and Germination-born (*Udbhijja*). Found throughout classic poetry metrics (*Kumārasambhava*). [cite: 341, 342, 582]
5. **Gāyatrī:** Technically translated contextually here as Catechu wood (*Khādira*) formations (*Nighaṇṭuśeṣa* 1.64). [cite: 366]
```

# SAMARĀNGANA-SŪTRADHĀRA
### of Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva Paramāra

---

## CONCLUSION OF CHAPTER 4: Mahadādi-Sarga

ज्ञात्वैनां पुरुषः पुण्यां भवति स्वर्गभाजनम्।
भुवनभूजलवह्निमरुद्वियत्प्रमुख एष भवस्तव कीर्त्तितः।
वसुमतीपरिमाणविनिश्चयं कथयतः शृणु सम्प्रति वत्स ! मे।॥३८॥

Having known this the sacred one the man becomes an object of Heaven [cite: 741]. The universe, the earth or ground, the water, the fire, the wind and the sky or atmosphere headed by these this creativity for you has been declaimed [cite: 742]. The extent of the earth its determination, Oh child, you may hear now, when I am talking of it [cite: 743].

---

इति महाराजाधिराजश्रीभोजदेवविरचिते समराङ्गणसूत्रधारापरनाम्नि वास्तुशास्त्रेमहदादिसर्गाध्यायश्चतुर्थः।।४।।
*(Thus ends the fourth chapter named Mahadādi-Sarga in the Vāstuśāstra text, otherwise known as Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra, composed by Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva.)* [cite: 744]

---

## CHAPTER 5: Bhuvana-kośa¹
### (The Description of the Earth and Cosmography)

अथो यथाक्रमं भूमेः कृत्स्नायाः कथयामि ते।
विष्कम्भपरिधी वत्स ! बाहुल्यमपि च स्फुटम्।।१।।

Now as per serial order I shall dilate upon Aye child! the extension or length and circumference or periphery or epicycle as also the dimensions of the whole earth [cite: 749, 750].

---

विष्कम्भोऽस्याः समुद्दिष्टो दशयोजनकोटयः ।
लक्षाण्यपि च मेदिन्यास्तद्वदेकोनविंशतिः ।
विष्कम्भत्रिगुणो यावद् विष्कम्भांशश्च पञ्चमः ॥२॥
मेदिन्याः परिधिस्तावद्योजनैः परिकीर्त्तितः ।
द्वात्रिंशत्कोटयः षष्टिर्लक्षाणि परिधिः क्षितेः॥३॥

The extension (*Vişkambha*²) of the earth stands enunciated as ten crores of yojanas with lacs amounting to nineteen [cite: 754]. Three times³ more than the extension added by a fifth portion of the extension, the circumference of the earth extending to that many yojanas stands confirmed: thirty two crores and sixty lacs of (yojanas) is the circumference of the earth [cite: 755].

---

अशीतिश्च सहस्त्राणि योजनानां प्रकीर्त्तितः।
योजनानां सहस्त्राणि विंशतिर्लक्षयोर्द्वयम् ।।४।।
इति बाहुल्यमेतस्याः क्षितेर्वत्स ! तवोदितम्।
चतुर्णां सलिलादीनां भूतादेर्महतोऽपि च।।५।।
उत्तरोत्तरमुर्वीतो मानं शतगुणं विदुः ।
तोयादिषु स्थितेयं भूश्चक्रवद् वृत्तशालिनी ॥६॥

Added on to these, eighty thousand of yojanas are enunciated as such [cite: 766]. The twenty thousands of yojanas and two lacs or lac twain is the *bāhulya*⁴ or area superficial contents of this one, Oh child [cite: 767]! This has been told to you as such of the four elements (such as water, fire, wind etc.) and of the *Mahat* headed by *Bhūta* (i.e. *ākāśa*) and the like; even one after the other following the earth, the measurement is known as a hundred fold [cite: 768]. This earth is stationary in waters having the glamour globular like a circle or wheel [cite: 769].

---

पात्रस्थापरपात्रश्रीहारीण्यन्यान्यपि क्रमात्।
प्रमाणमिदमेतेषां क्षित्यादीनां तवोदितम्।।७।।

Just as a pot within a pot having the glory of one wrested by the other affords an appearance (i.e. as one pot), likewise the structure of this earth is of the same type in due course of viability [cite: 772]. Therefore the extent of the earth stands illustrated before you [cite: 773].

---

द्वीपदीनां तु पाथोधिनिवेशः पुनरुच्यते ।
द्वीपानामम्बुधीनां च सप्तानामपि मध्यगः ।।८।।
जम्बूद्वीपो भवेद् वृत्तः सहस्त्रशतविस्तृतः ।
हिमाद्रिर्हेमकूटाख्यो निषधो नीलसंज्ञितः ।।९।।
श्वेतः शृङ्गी च षडमी भवन्त्यस्मिन् कुलाचलाः।

Of the islands, the ocean as the receptacle is being illustrated and gone within the centre of the seven islands and the oceans [cite: 776]. Jambūdvīpa may be the one having circular form extended to a hundred thousands (of yojanas) [cite: 780]. Himadri (Himalaya), and the one Hemakūta by name, Nişadha, and the one called Nīla, Śveta and Śrngi — those six as such stand defined as hereditary mountains (*Kulācalas*) [cite: 780].

---

एतस्मादुत्तरेणाद्रेस्तुषाराङ्कितमेखलात् ।।१०।।
पूर्वापरायताः सर्वेऽप्यद्र्यो यावदम्बुधि।
अन्तरा नीलनिषधौ जम्बूद्वीपस्य नाभिगः ।।११।।
वृत्तः पुण्यजनाकीर्णः श्रीमान् मेरुर्महाचलः।

To the north of this mountain having slopes covered (lit. marked by snow) [cite: 781], extended in East and West, all the mountains even down to the ocean stand [cite: 782]; and in between Nīla and Nişadha gone within the navel [cite: 784, 785], circular globular as such and inhabited by the *Punyajanas* (Yakṣas⁵), endowed with glory or beauty, is Meru the great mountain [cite: 786, 790].

---

उदग्याम्यायते मेरोः प्राग्भागे माल्यवान् गिरिः ।।१२।।
सेवितः सिद्धनारीभिरानीलनिषधायतः ।
सुमेरोः पश्चिमेनाद्रिर्गन्धर्वकुलसङ्कुलः।।१३॥

In the north-southern stretched out frontal part (*Prāgbhāga*) of Meru, there is the Mālyavān mountain [cite: 790], waited upon by the Siddha damsels and extended upto Nila and Nisadha [cite: 791]. To the west of Sumeru is the mountain Gandhamādana, crowded by Gandharva clans [cite: 792, 793].

---

माल्यवत्सदृशायामो महीभृद् गन्धमादनः ।
पर्वताबुभयान्तस्थौ हिमवान् शृङ्गवांस्तथा।।१४।।
योजनानां सहस्त्रे द्वे सार्धे स्यादुच्छ्रयस्तयोः ।
श्वेतश्च हेमकूटश्चेत्यन्तयोः पृथिवीधरौ ।। १५ ।।
योजनानां सहस्रार्धमेकैकस्योच्छ्रयस्तयोः।

The two mountains situated in the space between these two, are Himavān (i.e. Himālaya) and Śrngavān [cite: 794]. And of these two the height is two and a half thousands of yojanas [cite: 797]. Śveta and Hemakūta mountains are situated on the intermediary space of these two [cite: 799, 800]. Of each one of these two the height is five hundred yojanas [cite: 801].

---

निषधाचलनीलाद्रिमाल्यवद्गन्धमादनाः ।। १६ ।।
सहस्रयोजनोच्छ्रायाश्चत्वारोऽमी पृथक्पृथक्।
एतेऽष्टावपि शैलेन्द्राः सहस्त्रद्वयविस्तृताः ।।१७।।
उच्छ्रयार्थमधश्चापि विलग्नाः सह मेरुणा।

Nişadha mountain, the Nila mountain, Malyavān and Gandhamadana are a thousand yojanas in height, the four as such existing separate [cite: 805, 815]. These eight mountains are two thousand yojanas in extension [cite: 816], and half in height even below stand clung on along with Meru [cite: 817].

---

मेरोः समुच्छ्रयोऽशीतिः सहस्त्राणि चतुर्युता ।।१८।।
षोडशाधः सहस्त्राणि द्वात्रिंशन्मूर्ध्नि विस्तृतिः ।
जम्बूतरुर्महान् मध्ये सुमेरोर्निषधस्य च।।१९।।
द्वीपस्यामुष्य यद्योगाज्जम्बूद्वीप इति श्रुतिः ।

And the height of Meru is eighty thousand added by four (84,000) yojanas [cite: 819]. And below sixteen thousand and on the top thirty two thousand of yojanas is the extension or extensiveness [cite: 820]; and in between the Sumeru and Nişadha, a Jambu tree, the huge one, stands as such [cite: 820]. On account of the affiliation of this very tree, Jambūdvīpa or Island stands named as such; such a popularity is in vogue [cite: 822].

---

शृङ्गैर्हिमशिलानद्वैः सर्वतो हिमवानयम्।।२०।।
महान्तो निवसन्त्यत्र पिशाचा यक्षराक्षसाः।
कूटैर्हेममयैर्हेमकूट इत्यवनीधरः ।।२१।।
यं सर्वतो निषेवन्ते सदा चारणगुह्यकाः।

And by the peaks strung up with snow slabs all around stands Himavān i.e. Himālaya [cite: 823]. Stupendous figured abide here: the Piśācas, Yaksas and Rākṣasas [cite: 826]. And with peaks made of Hema (i.e. gold), Hemakūța, this one was known as the mountain [cite: 827], to which serve perennially or to which keep occupied perennially Cāraṇas (heavenly charioteers⁶) and Guhyakas [cite: 828, 830].

---

तरुणार्कप्रभाजालप्रतिमो निषधाचलः ।।२२।॥
निवसन्ति सुखं तत्र शेषवासुकितक्षकाः ।
हेमाब्जकर्णिकाकारः सुमेरुर्मणिकन्दरः ।।२३।।
अत्रामराः साप्सरसस्त्रयस्त्रिंशद् वसन्ति ते।

There is the Nișadha mountain, a compeer to the network of fresh solar rays [cite: 830]. Abide along there cosily: Śeşa (nāga), Vāsuki and Takşaka [cite: 831, 833]. Sumeru has bejewelled grottoes having the shape of the pericarp of a golden lotus [cite: 833, 834]. Here do abide the gods (*Amaras*), thirty-three in number, along with the nymphs [cite: 835].

---

वैडूर्यनद्वैः शिखरैर्नीलो नीलमहीधरः ।।२४।।
कलयन्ति तपोनित्या यत्र ब्रह्मर्षयः स्थितिम्।
श्वेतः स काञ्चनैः शृङ्गैर्गगनोल्लेखिभिर्वृतः।। २५॥
दोर्दर्पशालिनां यत्र निवासस्त्रिदशद्विषाम्।

Overladen by the peaks inlaid by Turquoise or lapis lazuli is the azure-hued Nila mountain [cite: 840], where assume abode the sages unending in austerities (*Brahmarṣis*) [cite: 841]. Śveta mountain with golden peaks, the sky-scraping ones, stands encompassed all over [cite: 842], wherein is the abode of the enemies of gods (*Tridaśadviṣām*) englamoured by the prowess of arms [cite: 843].

---

महानीलमयो बर्हिपिच्छच्छायो बहिर्महान्।।२६।।
पितृणामालयः शृङ्गैरुच्छ्रितैः शृङ्गवान् गिरिः।
हिमाचलस्य याम्येन क्षाराब्धिवृतमन्यतः ।।२७।।
वर्षं स्याद् भारतं नाम प्रथमं कार्मुकाकृति।

The one made of sapphire stones, a huge one having the shade of the peacock's plumes, is the mountain Śrigavān, the very resort of the manes (*Pitṛs*), with lofty peaks [cite: 844, 846]. Through the southern direction of Himalaya, surrounded by the salt ocean from the other side [cite: 846, 847], is the Varșa named "Bhārata", the very primeval one, having the shape of an arc or bow [cite: 848, 851].

---

तुषारनिलयस्याद्रेर्हेमकूटाचलस्य च।॥२८॥
मध्ये किंपुरुषं नाम द्वितीयं वर्षमीरितम्।
अन्तरे हेमकूटस्य निषधस्य च भूभृतः ॥२९॥
हरिवर्षमिति प्रोक्तं तृतीयं वर्षमुत्तमम्।

And in the middle of the mountain being a store house of snow (Himalaya) and the mountain Hemakūta, the second varșa named Kimpuruşa stands extended [cite: 852]. In between the Hemakūta and Nişadha mountains, "Harivarsa" is proclaimed as the third varșa, the best one [cite: 853, 856].

---

निषधाचलनीलाद्रिमाल्यवद्गन्धभूभृताम् ।।३०।।
चतुर्णां मध्यगं वर्षं तुर्यमस्िन्त्रलावृतम्।
उत्तरे नीलशैलस्य याम्ये च श्वेतभूभृतः ।।३१।।
पञ्चमं वर्षमत्यर्थरम्यं रम्यकसंज्ञितम्।

Gone in the middle of the four mountains Nişadha, Nīla, Mālyavān and Gandhamādana, the fourth varșa herein is "Ilāvṛta" [cite: 857]. In the north of Nila mountain and to the south of Śveta mountain, the fifth varșa, highly gorgeous, is known as Ramyaka [cite: 857, 861, 863].

---

श्वेतशृङ्गवतोः शैलराजयोरनयोरिह।। ३२ ।।
मध्ये षष्ठं हिरण्यांशुरम्यं हैरण्यकाह्वयम्।
अस्योत्तरे शृङ्गवतो याम्ये च क्षारवारिघेः क्षारवारिघेः क्षारवारिघेः ।।३३॥
कुरुवर्षाभिधं वर्षमुत्तरेण प्रचक्षते ।

In the middle of Śrnga mountain and Śveta mountain, here is the varșa named Hairanyaka, the sixth one, lovely like the network of golden beams [cite: 863]. In the north of this one and in the southern quarter of the salt ocean, Kuruvarșa, named as such, is called the northern one (the seventh one) [cite: 864, 867].

---

अन्तरा नीलनिषधौ प्राग्भागे माल्यवगिरेः ॥ ३४।।
भद्राश्वमष्टमं वर्षं प्राक्समुद्रान्तमीरितम्।
गन्धमादनशैलस्य प्रत्यक् प्राक् चापराम्बुधेः ।॥३५॥
नवमं वर्षमाचार्याः केतुमालं प्रचक्षते।

In the forepart of the Malyavān mountain are Nīla and Nișadha in between [cite: 868]: Bhadrāśva varșa, the eighth one, stands stretched upto the ends of the eastern ocean [cite: 871]. To the west of Gandhamādana mountain and to the east of the western ocean, the Ācāryas call as Ketumāla, the ninth varșa [cite: 872, 873]. This way have been declaimed those nine varșas before you [cite: 874].

---

साम्प्रतं पुनरेतेषां प्रमाणमवधारय।
प्रमाणेन सहस्राणि चतुस्त्रिंशच्चतुर्दिशम् ।। ३७।।
योजनानामिहेच्छन्ति चतुरश्रमिलावृतम्।
प्राक्प्रत्यग्भागगे वर्षे तस्योदग्याम्यतः समे।। ३८ ।।
एकत्रिंशत्सहस्त्राणि किञ्चित् प्राक्प्रत्यगायते।

Now you may take into consideration the extent of these: by extensiveness, thirty four thousand of yojanas in the four quarters do they take note of the square-shaped Ilāvṛta [cite: 876, 878, 880]. In the varṣas extending towards the east and the west, and to the north and south of that one being equal in extent, it is thirty one thousand yojanas, somewhat elongated in longitude east and west [cite: 882, 884].

---

यान्युक्तानि षडन्यानि वर्षाण्येभ्योऽवराणि ते।।३९॥
तेषां नवसहस्राणि प्रत्येकं विस्तृतिर्मता।
वर्षे किम्पुरुषे नार्यो नराश्च प्लक्षभोजनाः ।॥४०॥
जीवन्त्ययुतमब्दानां जात्यजाम्बूनदत्विषः ।

Whichever have been declaimed as the other ones, the six other varṣas are quite of a smaller size than these [cite: 885, 889]. Of those, nine thousand yojanas is recognised as the extension of each [cite: 891]. In the varṣa named Kimpuruşa, the ladies and gents are inured to eating *Plakṣa*⁷ [cite: 893, 894], and live upto the span of ten thousand years, being by complexion of burnished gold colour [cite: 895, 897].

---

हरिवर्षे नरा नार्यो वसन्तीक्षुरसाशिनः ।।४१।।
सायुतं च सहस्रं ते जीवन्ति रजतत्विषः।
इलावृते नराः पद्मरागभासोद्गतास्तथा।।४२।।
जम्बूफलरसाहाराः सपादायुतजीविनः ।

In the Harivarșa, the men and women live having been fed on sugarcane juice [cite: 898]. Silvery white complexioned, they live to the span of eleven thousand (11,000) years [cite: 899, 901]. In the Ilāvrta varșa, the men emerge with topaz or ruby-like complexions [cite: 902]; they have food from the rose-apple fruit juice (*Jambū-phala*) and live up to twelve and a half thousand years [cite: 903, 905].

---

नास्मिन् मेरुतटच्छन्ने तारकार्केन्दुरश्मयः ।॥४३॥
स्वाङ्गप्रभाभिः किन्त्वत्र कृतोद्योता वसन्त्यमी।
कैरवोदरसच्छाया भद्राश्वे साङ्गना नराः ।।४४।।
नीलाम्रकफलाहारा भवन्त्यत्रायुतायुषः ।

In this one covered by the surface of Meru, the rays of the sun, moon, and stars are conspicuous by their absence [cite: 906]. But by the gleam of their personal bodies having illumination offered, they keep on living [cite: 907]. In Bhadrāśva, the men and women have a complexion like the hollow of a white lotus [cite: 908, 909]; they feed on blue mango fruit and live an age equal to twenty thousand years [cite: 910, 911].

---

दलत्कुवलयश्यामाः केतुमाले शरीरिणः ।॥४५॥
शारदामयुतं तेषां आयुः पनसभोजिनाम्।
श्वेताभो रम्यके रम्ये न्यग्रोधफलभुग् जनः।।४६।।
हरिवर्ष इव प्रोक्तमेतस्मिन् मानमायुषः।

Azure-hued like the blowing blue lotus are the embodied ones in Ketumāla [cite: 911]. Their age is ten thousand autumns (*Śarads*), and they feed on *Panasa* (breadfruit) [cite: 915, 917]. In the lovely Ramyaka varșa, the population is white-complexioned and partakes of the fruit of the Banyan tree (*Nyagrodha*) [cite: 918]. The extent of age in this varșa stands enunciated like that of Harivarșa [cite: 921].

---

श्यामत्विषः स्त्रियो वर्षे पुमांसश्च हिरण्यके ।।४७।।
जीवन्त्ययुतमब्दानां सर्वेऽपि लकुचाशिनः ।
कुरुष्वभीष्टदैर्वृक्षैर्जीवन्ति स्त्रीयुता नराः ।।४८।।
सपादमयुतं देवगर्भभा गौरकान्तयः।

Dark complexioned are the ladies and men in the Hiranyakavarșa [cite: 922]. They live up to ten thousand years, all being partakers of *Lakuca* fruit [cite: 923]. ## ASTRONOMICAL MOVEMENTS AND COSMIC LEVEL MEASUREMENTS

स्थितिं गतिं च कथयाम्यर्कादीनामतः परम्।
सूर्येन्दुधिष्ण्यज्ञसितभौमार्कित्रिदशार्चिताः ।।८५ ।।
सप्तर्षयो ध्रुवश्चेति भूमेरूर्वं क्रमात् स्थिताः।

Above the earth are stationed in vertical layers: the Sun (*Arka*), the Moon (*Indu*), the Nakṣatras (*Dhiṣṇyas*), Mercury (*Jña*), Venus (*Sita*), Mars (*Bhauma*), Saturn (*Ārki*), Jupiter (*Tridaśārcitāḥ*), the Seven Sages (*Saptarṣi* / Ursa Major), and *Dhruva* (the Polar Star) [cite: 1079, 1082, 1096].

The intervals between these planetary spheres are traditionally calculated as a hundred thousand yojanas each [cite: 1083], while the higher levels up to Dhruva extend dynamically into millions of yojanas [cite: 1091]. Higher still are **Maharloka, Janaloka, Tapaloka, and Satyaloka**, situated below the outer boundary shell of the primordial egg (*Aṇḍakarpara*) [cite: 1107].

### METRIC REVOLUTIONS AND SPEED OF THE SUN
The Sun constantly revolves around Mount Meru on a single-wheeled chariot drawn by seven steeds [cite: 1121, 1123].
* **Daily Path Range**: Within a single day and night cycle, the hot-rayed sun traverses exactly **nine crores, ninety-seven lakhs, and fifty thousand yojanas** ($99,750,000 	ext{ yojanas}$) along its path over the concentric horizons [cite: 1141, 1144, 1154].
* **Exact Time Breakdown Fractions**: This reduces down sequentially to the baseline movement metrics evaluated by classical astronomers [cite: 1150]:
  * $246 \frac{8}{27} 	ext{ yojanas}$ per *nimeṣa* (moment) [cite: 1150].
  * $3,694 \frac{4}{9} 	ext{ yojanas}$ per *kāṣṭhā* [cite: 1150].
  * $110,833 \frac{1}{3} 	ext{ yojanas}$ per *kalā* (minute) [cite: 1153].
  * $3,325,000 	ext{ yojanas}$ per *muhūrtta* [cite: 1153].

गतिरपि दिनभर्तुः कीर्त्तिता विश्वमानं पुनरिह युगधर्मं कीर्त्यमानं निबोध ।।१०५॥

## THE BIRTH OF ARCHITECTURE: BUILDING THE FIRST HOMES

आधिभौतिकमप्यासीद् दुःखं व्यालमृगादिजम्।।३४।।

 Mortals found their physical frames invaded by diseases, systemic functional imbalances, and grief, while their minds became heavily polluted by lust, blinding rage, jealousy, and despair [cite: 1329]. They were assaulted by massive cosmic miseries (*Ādhidaivika*) brought on by scorching summer heat, freezing monsoons, and bitter cold, alongside terrestrial miseries (*Ādhibhautika*) inflicted by predatory beasts and venomous serpents [cite: 1334].

---

इत्थं दुःखत्रयार्त्तास्ते व्यवायाद्यभिगुप्तये।
हिमनीहारशीताम्बुवाताद्यापच्छिदेऽपि च ।।३५॥
अजातप्रीतयो वृक्षैः कुट्टिमानि गृहाणि (ते? च)।
व्यधुश्छित्त्वाश्मभिर्वृक्षानन्यान् दुःखार्तचेतसः ।। ३६।।

Tormented by this threefold structural misery (*Duḥkha-traya*), and desperate to protect the privacy of their physical copulations while escaping the volatile onslaughts of snow, frost, pouring rain, and violent gales, humans abandoned their open attachment to trees [cite: 1337, 1340]. Armed with stone axes, they began cutting down trees to clear land and construct the very first paved structures and houses [cite: 1340].

---

स्मृत्वा कल्पद्रुमाकारस्तद्रूपाणि गृहाणि ते।
एकद्वित्रिचतुः सप्तदशशालानि चक्रिरे ।।३७॥
श(ब्दा?  ) प्राकारपरिखेष्वाच्छन्नेषु तृणादिभिः ।
हृष्टास्तेष्वनयन् कालमाप्तेषु गृहमेधिनः ।।३८ ।।

Evoking the lingering memory of the balanced, branch-like geometric patterns of the lost *Kalpadruma* trees, they designed their homes based on those exact configurations [cite: 1343]. They built modular layouts classified into:
* **Eka-śāla** (Single-winged/one room) [cite: 1344]
* **Dvi-śāla** (Two-winged) [cite: 1344]
* **Tri-śāla** (Three-winged) [cite: 1344]
* **Catuḥ-śāla** (Four-winged/quadrangle houses) [cite: 1344]
* **Sapta-śāla** (Seven-winged) and **Daśa-śāla** (Ten-winged configurations) [cite: 1344].

Thatching their roofs with dense grass and reeds, and throwing up defensive perimeter walls (*Prākāra*) and deep protective moats (*Parikhā*), they transitioned joyfully into the structured lifestyle of established householders (*Gṛhamedhins*) [cite: 1347, 1348].

---

इत्यमीषु गृहिणो गृहेषु ते शीतवातजलतापनाशिषु।
हर्षसंवलितमानसाश्चिरं सन्निरस्तविपदोऽवसन् सुखम् ।।३९॥

Thus, ensconced safely within these newly engineered houses that completely warded off severe cold, violent winds, flooding rains, and scorching heat, human beings overthrew their immediate environmental perils and lived once more in comfort [cite: 1351].

---

इति महाराजाधिराजश्रीभोजदेवविरचिते समराङ्गणसूत्रधारापरनाम्नि वास्तुशास्त्रे सहदेवाधिकारो नाम षष्ठोऽध्यायः ।।
*(Thus ends the sixth chapter named Sahadevādhikāra in the Vāstuśāstra text, otherwise known as Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra, composed by Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva.)* [cite: 1352]

---

### CHAPTER 6 CRITICAL EXPLANATORY NOTES

1. **Sahadevādhikāra / Bhavana Janma Kathā**: This chapter explains the transition of mankind from divine cohabitation to physical mortality, presenting an architectural origin story. While Dr. D.N. Shukla titles it *Bhavana Janma Kathā* ("The Story of the Birth of Buildings"), the literal title *Sahadevādhikāra* relates to the baseline evolution of mortals alongside gods, tracking cosmic shifts similar to the *Nāsadīya Sūkta* (Rgveda X.129) [cite: 1207].
2. **Helayā**: Denotes effortless celestial flight or amorous, amoral dalliance native to the uncorrupted mind prior to systemic shame [cite: 1208].
3. **Bhūrasa**: The primordial sweet sap or crystalline baseline nutrient exuded directly by the early crust of the earth, often compared to high concentrated sugarcane (*Ikṣu*) expressions (*Bhāvaprakāśa-nighaṇṭu*) [cite: 1217, 1229, 1230].
4. **Kavarī**: Refers to dense, decorative, intertwined braided tresses—used as an elegant metaphor for the heavy, interlocking dark storm clouds of the early era [cite: 1226, 1233].
5. **Urban Typologies Lexicon**:
   * **Kheṭa**: A small village outpost occupied mainly by peasant-agriculturists [cite: 1247].
   * **Nagara**: A city center explicitly backed by or structured directly around defensive rocky terrain/mountains [cite: 1247, 1252].
   * **Grāma**: A cluster of houses arranged over stone-paved spaces or shared common resources [cite: 1247, 1253].
   * **Pura**: A heavy urban fortress complete with thick masonry walls and deep perimeter moats measuring at least one *Krośa* in standard length [cite: 1255].
```

## CHAPTER 7: Varṇāśrama-Pravibhāga
### (The Segregation of Varṇas and Āśramas / The Orders of Society & Stages of Life)

अथामरगणैः सार्धमाजगाम पितामहः।
दुःखच्छेदाय मर्त्यानामादाय नृपतिं पृथुम् ।।१।।

Then along with the hosts of gods came Pitāmaha (i.e. Brahmā) for the sake of obviating the grief of mortals, bringing along the Lord of men, King Pṛthu [cite: 2736, 2737].

---

स तानूचे प्रभुर्वोऽसौ मरुतामिव वासवः।
दण्डधारी च दुष्टानां प्रभावे लोकपालवत्।।२।।

He spoke to them: "He is your Lord, just as Vāsava (Indra) is to the gods, bearing the sceptre or rod for the control of the wicked, equal in authority to a *Lokapāla* (the guardians of the quarters¹) [cite: 2740, 2742]."

---

प्रतापतापितारातिसिंहः सिंहपराक्रमः ।
युष्माकमाधिपत्येऽसावभिषिक्तो मया पृथुः ॥३॥

"Having lions in the form of enemies tormented by his prowess, Pṛthu, being one who has the might of a lion, has been consecrated by me over your administrative organization [cite: 2744, 2746]."

---

रक्षाकृत् सर्वशिष्टानामुच्छेत्ता दुष्टचेतसाम्।
वृत्तितो भीतिहर्ता च भविष्यत्येष वो नृपः।।४।।

"As a guardian of all sophisticated, righteous beings and an extirpator of the wicked-hearted, this king shall become the assuager of your structural fear [cite: 2748, 2750]."

---

भवद्भिरेतदायत्तैर्भवितव्यं ममाज्ञया।
करिष्यत्येष वो नीत्या चातुर्वर्ण्यश्रमस्थितीः ।।५।।

"By my command, you must remain obedient to him. By diplomatic and righteous moves, he shall organize and sustain the status of the four *Varṇas* (orders of society) and *Āśramas* (stages of life) [cite: 2751, 2754]."

---

उक्त्वेति ब्रह्मणि गतेनाथ मासाद्य तेऽथ तम्।
अवोचन् दुःखिता दुःखादस्मात् त्रायस्व नः प्रभो !।।६॥
कल्पद्रुमामरत्यक्तान् द्वन्द्वार्तिक्लान्तचेतसः ।
व्यसनार्णवनिर्मग्नान् पाहि नः पृथिवीपते ! ।।॥७।।

Having spoken thus, when Brahmā departed, the aggrieved people approached the new master and spoke out of intense agony: "Oh Lord! Rescue us. Missing the wish-granting trees, abandoned by the gods, our hearts are weary from the opposite dualities of existence and sunk deep into this ocean of calamity. Protect us, Oh Lord of the Earth! [cite: 2755, 2756, 2765, 2766]"

---

अथो पृथुरुवाचैतान् मा भैष्ट सुखमास्यताम्।
दुःखान् अपहरिष्यामि करिष्ये च सुखानि वः।।८।।

Then Pṛthu reassured them: "Be not afraid; reside at ease. I shall alleviate your sorrows, remove your inconveniences, and ensure your comforts [cite: 2768, 2770]."

## THE STRATIFICATION OF THE FOUR VARNAS (SOCIETY ORDERS)

ततः स चतुरो वर्णानाश्रमांश्च व्यभाजयत्।
तेषु ये वेदनिरताः स्वाचाराः संयतेन्द्रियाः ।।९।।
सूरयश्चावदाताश्च ब्राह्मणास्तेऽभवंस्तदा।
यजनाध्ययने दानं याजनाध्यापनार्थिताः ।। १० ।।

Then he systematically allocated the jurisdictions of the four orders of society and the four stages of life [cite: 2771].
* **The Brāhmaṇas**: Those among them who were devoted to wisdom, continuous learning, and the Vedas, who were well-demeaned, tidy, and controlled in their senses, became the Brāhmaṇas [cite: 2774, 2775]. Their duties comprised performance of sacrifices (*Yajana*), studying (*Adhyayana*), giving charity (*Dāna*), officiating over sacrifices for others (*Yājana*), and teaching (*Adhyāpana*) [cite: 2776, 2777].

---

ये तु शूरा महोत्साहाः शरण्या रक्षणक्षमाः ।।११।।
दृढव्यायतदेहष्च क्षत्रियास्त इहाभवन्।
विक्रमो लोकसंरक्षाविभागो व्यवसायिता ।।१२।।

* **The Kṣatriyas**: Those who were chivalrous, highly courageous (*Mahotsāha*), fit to afford refuge, capable of rescue operations, and possessed stout, tall-statured bodies, became the Kṣatriyas [cite: 2778, 2781]. Their ordained track focused on physical strength, martial prowess, absolute protection of the people, administration, and professional perseverance [cite: 2781].

---

निसर्गान्नैपुणं येषां रतिर्वित्तार्जनं प्रति ।।१३।।
श्रद्धादाक्ष्यदयावन्तो वैश्यांस्तानकरोदसौ।
चिकित्सा कृषिवाणिज्ये स्थापत्यं पशुपोषणम् ।।१४।॥

* **The Vaiśyas**: Those who by natural instinct possessed commercial skill, a penchant for generating wealth, and were endowed with deep faith, diligence, and compassion, he organized as the Vaiśyas [cite: 2786, 2789]. Their duties and means of living included medicine, agriculture (*Kṛṣi*), trade or commerce (*Vāṇijya*), craftsmanship or architecture (*Sthāpatya*), and animal husbandry [cite: 2790, 2791].

---

नातिमानभृतो नातिशुचयः पिशुनाश्च ये ।।१५।।
ते शूद्रजातयो जाता नातिधर्मरताश्च ये।
कलारम्भोपजीवित्वं शिल्पिता पशुपोषणम् ।। १६ ।।
वर्णत्रितयशुश्रूषा धर्मस्तेषामुदाहृतः ।

* **The Śūdras**: Those who did not possess high pride, were less fastidious about fastidious purity, and historically prone to minor discord, formed the Śūdra caste [cite: 2793, 2796]. Their livelihood was derived from artistic pursuits (*Kalā*), mechanical artisanship (*Śilpitā*), cattle-rearing, and rendering service (*Śuśrūṣā*) to the three higher orders [cite: 2797, 2799].

---

## THE FOUR ASHRAMAS (STAGES OF LIFE)

ब्रह्मचारी गृहस्थो वा वानप्रस्थस्तथा यतिः ।।१७।।
इत्याश्रमाः पृथक् तेन चत्वारः प्रविभाजिताः।

The four distinct stages of human life were systematically partitioned as follows [cite: 2801]:

1. **Brahmacārin (The Celibate Student)**: Focused on serving the teacher (*Guru-śuśrūṣā*), alms-begging (*Bhaiṣa*), strict vows, maintaining the sacred fire, meditation, study, and ritual bathing [cite: 2802, 2805].
2. **Gṛhastha (The Householder)**: Worship of fire, hospitality to guests and gods, sustaining life through honest personal earning (*Svavṛtti*), restraint, marriage into compatible non-related lineage clans (*Asamāna-gotra*), marital fidelity, and general benevolence [cite: 2806, 2813, 2814, 2815].
3. **Vānaprastha (The Forest Hermit)**: Donning barks and animal hides, growing matted hair, sleeping on the bare ground, attenuating the body through rigorous fasts, and subsisting solely on forest food grown without tillage [cite: 2820, 2822, 2824].
4. **Yati / Sannyāsin (The Wandering Renunciant)**: Absolute renunciation, mastery of the senses, complete abandonment of anxiety, perfect internal tranquility, total poverty (*Ākiñcanya*), and constant meditation [cite: 2825, 2827].

---

स्वधर्मावस्थितानां वो भावि लोकद्वये सुखम्।
य एतां स्थितिमुल्लङ्घय मोहादन्यद् विधास्यति ।। २८॥
तस्याहं यमवत् क्रुद्धः करिष्याम्यनुशासनम्।

King Pṛthu decreed: "For all of you who stay stable in your respective duties, bliss is guaranteed in both worlds [cite: 2847, 2849]. But whoever transgresses this status out of infatuation, I shall punish and discipline them, raging like Yama [cite: 2850, 2851]."

---

## THE LEVELING OF THE EARTH FOR SETTLEMENTS

खेटकग्रामवेश्मानि विधास्यामि पुराणि च।
इत्युक्त्वा तानथो कोट्या कार्मुकस्य पृथुर्नृपः ।।३०।।
विषमां साधयामास पृथिवीं पृथुविक्रमः ।

Declaring "I shall construct residential abodes, *Kheṭas*, *Grāmas*, and *Puras*," the mighty King Pṛthu took up his bow [cite: 2855, 2856, 2857]. With the curved tip of his bow (*Dhanuṣkoṭi*), he leveled the rugged, uneven mountain terrains of the wild Earth to make it fit for human architecture and agriculture [cite: 2858, 2859]. Driven to distress, the Earth assumed the form of a cow and fled, but by natural cosmic law, she eventually yielded and was milked, shedding rich grain and crops for the welfare of mankind [cite: 2860, 2861, 2865, 2867].

---

इति महाराजाधिराजश्रीभोजदेवविरचिते समराङ्गणसूत्रधारापरनाम्नि वास्तुशास्त्रे वर्णाश्रमप्रविभागो नाम सप्तमोऽध्यायः ।।
*(Thus ends the seventh chapter named Varṇāśrama-pravibhāga in the Vāstuśāstra text, otherwise known as Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra, composed by Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva.)* [cite: 2893]

Vedia) analyze the Pṛthu-Vainya cycle as an astronomical allegory mapping cosmic thermodynamics [cite: 2879]. *Vainya* represents dynamic motion (from root *ven*, to contract/expand) [cite: 2916], while *Pṛthivī* represents structural expansion (from root *prath*, to expand) [cite: 2899, 2909]. The "milking of the earth cow" signifies establishing gravitational balance, planetary positioning, and structural alignment between *Agni* (active forces) and *Soma* (receptive forces) [cite: 2896, 2904].

## CHAPTER 8: Bhūmi-Parīkṣā
### (The Examination and Classification of Soil and Land)

देशः स्याज्जाङ्गलानूपसाधारणतया त्रिधा।
त्रिविधस्याप्यथैतस्य यथावल्लक्ष्म कथ्यते ।।२२।।

Territories are classified into three environmental typologies: **Jāṅgala** (arid/desert), **Ānūpa** (marshy/wetlands), and **Sādhāraṇa** (temperate/balanced) [cite: 2384, 2386].

* **Jāṅgala**: Characterized by scarce water tables located deep underground, saline soil (*Iriṇa*), short stunted thorny trees, fierce raucous winds, and a black soil base [cite: 2387, 2388, 2389].
* **Ānūpa**: Low-lying marshy ground, abounding in water, unctuous, teeming with fish, cold, with plentiful streams and humid, lofty, dense tree lines [cite: 2390, 2391, 2392].
* **Sādhāraṇa**: Neither too cold nor too hot, combining the healthy qualities of both zones into a temporally balanced environment [cite: 2393, 2395].

---

## THE SIXTEEN EXALTED LAND TYPES
Across these regions, lands are further sub-classified into sixteen distinct qualitative typologies for administration and settlement [cite: 2406, 2408]:

1. **Bāliśa-svāminī**: A secure land easily governed even by a young or novice ruler, populated by gentle folk [cite: 2420, 2421].
2. **Bhogyā**: Exceedingly affluent, generating steady revenue streams and yields (*Bhāga* and *Bhoga*) for its population [cite: 2424, 2433].
3. **Sītā-gocara-rakṣiṇī**: Rich crown lands punctuated by rivers and hills, offering natural protection for agricultural output and wandering cattle [cite: 2434, 2436].
4. **Apāśrayavatī**: A rugged, wild, or refugeless terrain bounded by deep forests and mountains where populations enter with awe [cite: 2437, 2439].
5. **Kāntā**: Exquisitely beautiful land, rich in gardens, orchards, and clear streams that delight the mind [cite: 2440, 2442].
6. **Khani-matī**: Ground rich in mineralogical resources, constantly yielding veins of gold, silver, structural metals, and salts [cite: 2443, 2445].
7. **Ātma-dhāriṇī**: Heavily self-sustaining and populous land that supports its people independently without requiring constant fiscal intervention [cite: 2447, 2453].
8. **Vaṇik-prasādhitā**: Strategically situated for commerce, bustling with market hubs, decorated and frequented by merchant caravans [cite: 2454, 2456].
9. **Dravyavatī**: Bounded by rich timber reserves containing valuable structural species like *Śāka* (Teak), *Aśvakarṇa*, *Khadira* (Catechu), *Syandana*, and structural reeds/canes [cite: 2457, 2459].
10. **Amitraghātinī**: Judiciously populated, free from internal strifes, where neighboring factions naturally maintain peaceful alliances [cite: 2461, 2462].
11. **Āśreṇī-puruṣā**: Populated by disciplined, self-governing communities requiring no punitive garrisons or forced labor camps [cite: 2464, 2481].
12. **Śakya-sāmantā**: Bounded by well-subordinated vassals and secondary chiefs who show complete allegiance to central counsel [cite: 2482, 2484].
13. **Deva-mātṛkā**: Highly fertile land fed independently by perennial rivers and mountain streams, requiring no anxious waiting for rainfall [cite: 2485, 2487].
14. **Dhānyā**: Blessed with rich soil where seeds sprout effortlessly, yielding luxuriant grain harvests [cite: 2488, 2490].
15. **Hastivanopetā**: Flanked by mountain frontiers and deep elephant sanctuaries, ensuring a steady supply of war tuskers to swell the king's army [cite: 2491, 2493].
16. **Surakṣā**: Naturally fortified and virtually irrepressible by enemies due to impassable rocky massifs and deep, un-wadable torrents [cite: 2494, 2496].

---

## CRITERIA FOR FORTRESS SITING (DURGA-BHŪMI)
Four types of terrain are specifically praised as ideal foundations for building protective military strongholds [cite: 2570, 2571]:
* **Giri-durga (Hill Fort)**: Located on high, water-endowed mountain peaks with sheer vertical rock faces that look as if chiselled out by a tool [cite: 2572, 2573].
* **Mūla-durga (Forest Fort)**: Bounded by deep, impenetrable thorny jungles, shrouded in shadow, with highly concealed labyrinthine entrance paths [cite: 2578, 2579].
* **Jala-durga (Water Fort)**: Positioned on open island systems surrounded by wide, plunging, un-wadable bodies of deep water [cite: 2581, 2583].

---

## QUANTITATIVE LAND TESTING METHODS

### Soil Allocation by Caste (Varna Colors and Tastes)
* **Brāhmaṇas**: White soil, sweet (*Madgura*) to taste, smelling of cow's milk or clarified butter [cite: 2607, 2609, 2620].
* **Kṣatriyas**: Red soil, astringent (*Kaṣāya*) to taste, smelling of biological energy or weapons [cite: 2607, 2609, 2620].
* **Vaiśyas**: Yellow soil, pungent (*Kaṭuka*) to taste, smelling of grains or commerce [cite: 2607, 2609, 2620].
* **Śūdras**: Black soil, bitter (*Tikta*) to taste, smelling of manual inputs [cite: 2607, 2609, 2620].

---

### Test 1: Pit Refilling (Volumetric Density Analysis)
Dig a precise cubit-sized square pit (*Khāta*) in the center of the site [cite: 2683, 2684]. Remove all the soil, then tightly shovel it back into the pit [cite: 2688, 2690]:
* **Uttama (Excellent/Best)**: Soil overflows the pit, indicating low compaction and rich organic density [cite: 2689].
* **Madhyama (Mediocre)**: Soil exactly fills the pit perfectly to the brim [cite: 2689].
* **Adhama (Inferior/Rejected)**: Soil falls short, leaving a void at the top, indicating sterile, highly porous earth [cite: 2692].

---

### Test 2: Water Absorption Rate
Fill the excavated pit completely to the brim with clear water [cite: 2700]. Walk exactly one hundred steps away and then return [cite: 2700, 2702]:
* **Auspicious**: The water level remains virtually constant, indicating excellent clay moisture retention properties [cite: 2703, 2704].
* **Inauspicious/Rejected**: The water drains out completely into the loose subsoil, proving the foundation is unsafe for heavy stone buildings [cite: 2704].

---

### Test 3: Floral and Lamp Longevity Testing
* **Floral Test**: Place different colored fresh flower wreaths in the pit overnight. Soil that keeps the flowers from wilting indicates a thriving environment suited for the corresponding societal division [cite: 2705, 2707].
* **Lamp Test**: Light oil lamps in small niches facing the four directions. The quarter where the lamp burns longest indicates the most auspicious zone for that sector's development [cite: 2709, 2716].

---

इति महाराजाधिराजश्रीभोजदेवविरचिते समराङ्गणसूत्रधारापरनाम्नि वास्तुशास्त्रे भूमिपरीक्षा नामाष्टमोऽध्यायः।।८।।
*(Thus ends the eighth chapter named Bhūmi-parīkṣā in the Vāstuśāstra text, otherwise known as Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra, composed by Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva.)* [cite: 2728]
```

# SAMARĀNGANA-SŪTRADHĀRA
### of Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva Paramāra
