## CHAPTER 9: Hasta-Lakṣaṇam
### (The Metrology of Linear Standards and Time Measurements)

हेतुः समस्तवास्तूनामाधारः सर्वकर्मणाम्।
मानोन्मानविभागादिनिर्णयैकनिबन्धनम्।।१।।

Linear metrology is the fundamental baseline of all architectural designs, the support of all functional crafts, and the sole analytical metric for structural measurements and weights (*Unmāna*) [cite: 2087, 2088].

---

## THE LINEAR SCALE OF METROLOGICAL EVOLUTION
The absolute baseline metrics used by ancient architects evolve sequentially from microscopic particles up to standard lengths [cite: 2094, 2104]:

| Metric Step | Sanskrit Term | Equivalency Definition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | **Paramāṇu** | Microscopic dust particle visible only in window sunbeams [cite: 2095] |
| 2 | **Rajas** | $8 	imes 	ext{Paramāṇu}$ [cite: 2105, 2106] |
| 3 | **Bālāgra** | $8 	imes 	ext{Rajas}$ (width of a single hair-tip) [cite: 2107, 2113] |
| 4 | **Likṣā** | $8 	imes 	ext{Bālāgra}$ (size of a nit) [cite: 2108, 2114] |
| 5 | **Yūkā** | $8 	imes 	ext{Likṣā}$ (size of a louse) [cite: 2109, 2115] |
| 6 | **Yava (Barley-corn)** | $8 	imes 	ext{Yūkā}$ [cite: 2110, 2116] |
| 7 | **Aṅgula (Finger-breadth)**| $8 	imes 	ext{Yava}$ (Standard unit = approx. 0.75 inches) [cite: 2112, 2117, 2142] |

---

## THREE VARIETIES OF THE CUBIT (HASTA / KARA)
A single standard standard *Hasta* (cubit) is defined as exactly **twenty-four finger-breadths** (*Aṅgulas*) [cite: 2122], representing the distance from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger [cite: 2102]. Depending on the size of the grain base used, it resolves into three operational lengths [cite: 2121, 2123]:

1. **Jyeṣṭha (Prāśaya) Hasta**: Constructed from Aṅgulas spanning exactly 8 structural grains wide ($24 	imes 8 = 192 	ext{ grains}$) [cite: 2121, 2221, 2224]. Used for surveying towns (*Puras*), *Kheṭas*, *Grāmas*, roads, canals, fields, and major long-distance pathways (*Yojana, Krośa, Gavyūti*) [cite: 2230, 2234, 2238].
2. **Madhyama (Sādhāraṇa) Hasta**: Constructed from Aṅgulas spanning exactly 7 structural grains wide ($24 	imes 7 = 168 	ext{ grains}$) [cite: 2121, 2223, 2226]. Used for manufacturing weapons, mechanical artillery, staves, royal vehicles (*Yānas*), dining couches, and ceremonial seats [cite: 2239, 2240].
3. **Kaniṣṭha (Mātrāśaya) Hasta**: Constructed from Aṅgulas spanning exactly 6 structural grains wide ($24 	imes 6 = 144 	ext{ grains}$) [cite: 2121, 2229, 2236]. Used for building deep wells, small tanks, structural machinery, sugarcane crushers, canoes, flags, umbrellas, and textile crafts [cite: 2241, 2243, 2244, 2252].

---

## WOOD SELECTION FOR MEASURING RODS
* **Recommended Woods**: Measuring staves must be constructed from rich, stiff, flawles timber like *Khadira* (Catechu), *Añjana*, or mature dense cane lines [cite: 2159, 2162].
* **Prohibited Defects**: Wood that is heavily knotted, hollowed, insect-eaten, cracked, old, or charred is strictly banned [cite: 2163, 2165].

---

## MODULE FRACTIONS DEFINED BY ANGULAS
Standard modular measurements are tracked according to the following metric scales [cite: 2256]:
* **Mātrā**: 1 *Aṅgula* [cite: 2257].
* **Kalā**: 2 *Aṅgulas* [cite: 2257].
* **Parva**: 3 *Aṅgulas* (finger-joints) [cite: 2260].
* **Muṣṭi**: 4 *Aṅgulas* (width of a closed fist) [cite: 2260, 2262].
* **Vitasti**: 12 *Aṅgulas* (span of a hand) [cite: 2266, 2276].
* **Ratni**: 21 *Aṅgulas* [cite: 2268].
* **Aratni**: 24 *Aṅgulas* (Standard Cubit) [cite: 2268, 2270].
* **Kṣiku**: 42 *Aṅgulas* [cite: 2269, 2271].
* **Danda / Dhanus**: 4 *Hastas* (approx. 6 feet) [cite: 2280, 2282, 2431].
* **Krośa**: 1,000 *Dhanus* [cite: 2281].
* **Yojana**: 4 *Gavyūtis* / 8,000 *Dhanus* (approx. 4.54 miles) [cite: 2284, 2289, 2438].

---

## MATHEMATICAL TIME COUNTING TAXONOMY
Time is systematically broken down according to dynamic structural fractions based on the wink of an eye [cite: 2306, 2349]:
* **1 Nimeṣa**: Single wink of a healthy eyelid [cite: 2308, 2349].
* **1 Kāṣṭhā**: $15 	imes 	ext{Nimeṣas}$ [cite: 2308, 2349].
* **1 Kalā**: $30 	imes 	ext{Kāṣṭhās}$ [cite: 2309, 2349].
* **1 Muhūrtta**: $30 	imes 	ext{Kalās}$ (approx. 48 minutes) [cite: 2309, 2349].
* **1 Ahorātra**: $30 	imes 	ext{Muhūrttas}$ (Full day and night cycle) [cite: 2309, 2349].
* **1 Pakṣa**: $15 	imes 	ext{Ahorātras}$ (Fortnight) [cite: 2311, 2351].
* **1 Māsa**: $2 	imes 	ext{Pakṣas}$ (Month) [cite: 2352, 2354].
* **1 Ṛtu**: $2 	imes 	ext{Māsas}$ (Season) [cite: 2352, 2354].
* **1 Ayana**: $3 	imes 	ext{Ṛtus}$ (Half-year/Sun's northern or southern course) [cite: 2353, 2354].
* **1 Vatsara**: $2 	imes 	ext{Ayanas}$ (Full Year) [cite: 2353, 2354].

---

इति महाराजाधिराजश्रीभोजदेवविरचिते समराङ्गणसूत्रधारापरनाम्नि वास्तुशास्त्रे हस्तलक्षणं नाम नवमोऽध्यायः ।॥९॥
*(Thus ends the ninth chapter named Hasta-lakṣaṇam in the Vāstuśāstra text, otherwise known as Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra, composed by Mahājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva.)* [cite: 2361]

## CHAPTER 10: Pura-Niveśa
### (The Layout, Founding, and Zoning of Cities)

पुरस्य त्रिविधस्यापि प्रमाणमथ कथ्यते ।
प्राकारपरिखाट्टालद्वाररथ्याध्वभिः सह ।।१।।

Urban engineering is organized according to explicit structural guidelines governing town scales, defensive perimeter walls (*Prākāra*), multi-layered moats (*Parikhā*), watchtowers (*Aṭṭālaka*), arched gateway systems (*Mahādvāra*), and central street grids [cite: 1405, 1406, 1407].

---

## THREE SCALES OF THE CITY (PURA)
The master layout of any urban center is defined along a tripartite baseline calculated via *Cāpas* (or *Dhanus* = 4 cubits/hastas) [cite: 1417, 1431]:

1. **Jyeṣṭha Pura (Large Capital)**: Bounded by a structural width of **4,000 Cāpas** ($16,000 	ext{ Hastas}$ / approx. 8,000 yards) [cite: 1417, 1419, 1438].
2. **Madhyama Pura (Middling Town)**: Bounded by a structural width of **2,000 Cāpas** ($8,000 	ext{ Hastas}$ / approx. 4,000 yards) [cite: 1418, 1420].
3. **Kaniṣṭha Pura (Small Settlement)**: Bounded by a structural width of **1,000 Cāpas** ($4,000 	ext{ Hastas}$ / approx. 2,000 yards) [cite: 1418, 1420, 1439].

---

## MASTER GRID CONFIGURATION & HIGHWAYS
Cities must be laid out on a perfect square grid matching the **Catusthaṣṭi-Pada Vāstu Mandala** (sixty-four plot matrix) [cite: 1425, 1430]. It features **six major avenues** (*Ṣaṭ-patha*) slicing north-south and east-west, establishing **nine large structural quadrants** (*Nava-catvara*) [cite: 1426, 1427].

### The Royal Highway (Rājamārga)
The grand central artery or spine of the town must be built aligned with the central grid axis [cite: 1448]:
* In large cities, its width spans exactly **twenty-four cubits** ($24 	ext{ Hastas}$) [cite: 1450, 1452].
* In middling cities, its width spans **twenty cubits** ($20 	ext{ Hastas}$) [cite: 1453].
* In small cities, its width spans **sixteen cubits** ($16 	ext{ Hastas}$) [cite: 1453].

The entire highway system must be perfectly leveled, stone-paved, and reinforced with a heavy gravel-tar layer (*Kāśma-śarkara*) to support the high friction of passing cavalry, war elephants, and royal chariots (*Caturaṅga-bala*) without breakdown [cite: 1455, 1456].

---

## THE DEFENSIVE ENVELOPE: MOATS AND RAMPARTS

### The Triad of Moats (Parikhā-Tritaya)
Directly on the exterior limits of the city, a system of **three massive, concentric moats** must be excavated [cite: 1501, 1513]. The trench floors are reinforced with dense masonry using cut stone blocks or burnt bricks [cite: 1514, 1515]. They are fed constantly via continuous stream current channels (*Vāgāminī-ambhas*) and equipped with functional flood sluices [cite: 1520, 1521].

### The Earth Rampart (Vapra)
The loose soil excavated from the moats is thrown up internally to construct a massive earth embankment [cite: 1507, 1510]. Its profile must be thoroughly rammed and trampled down by cattle hooves to assume a dense, curved profile resembling the back of a royal elephant (*Gaja-pṛṣṭha*) [cite: 1508, 1509].

### The Masonry Parapet Wall (Prākāra)
On top of this mud rampart, a thick masonry wall is erected, built from heavy stones or high-fired bricks [cite: 1528, 1529].
* **Width**: 12 cubits (Large), 10 cubits (Medium), or 8 cubits (Small) [cite: 1544, 1546].
* **Height**: Ranging strictly between 13 and 17 cubits. Even-numbered heights are forbidden by masters of the science [cite: 1551, 1553, 1554].
* **Coping**: The top features defensive crenellations shaped like monkey heads (*Kapi-śīrṣaka*) to protect archers [cite: 1558, 1562, 1564].

---

## WATCHTOWERS & COMBAT TURRETS (ATTALAKAS)
* **Structure**: Multi-level watchtowers are erected directly over the masonry wall, projecting outward to command lines of sight [cite: 1573, 1574].
* **Interval Spacing**: Towers are placed exactly **one hundred cubits apart** all along the perimeter, making the defense unscalable for opposing siege infantries or charging elephant brigades [cite: 1576, 1578, 1579].
* **Gate Defense (*Pratolīs*)**: Massive three-story defensive turrets are built over the main gates, heavily fortified with thick locking cross-bars, bolts, and deep wooden stakes (*Indrakīlas*) [cite: 1608, 1611, 1654, 1656]. Their upper roofs feature mechanical combat platforms loaded with heavy catapult machinery (*Yantras*), missile racks (*Astras*), and *Śataghnīs* (huge rolling spikes/iron bars) to repel frontal assaults [cite: 1647, 1648, 1653].

---

## INTERIOR ZONING AND CASTES SECTORIZATION
The internal sectors of the city are zoned relative to the cardinal and intermediate directions to ensure social, physical, and religious order [cite: 1804]:

* **The Core Center**: Reserved for the great temple of Brahmā (the lotus-born) and major administrative shrines for Indra, Balarāma, and Kṛṣṇa [cite: 1995, 1996, 1998].
* **North-East (Īśāna)**: Storage and trade of fine ghee, butter, and fresh fruits [cite: 1830].
* **East (Prācyā)**: The residential quarters of the **Kṣatriyas**, alongside the elite military commanders-in-chief and the vanguard [cite: 1832, 1834, 1852].
* **South-East (Āgneyī)**: Siting for gold artisans (*Suvarṇakāras*), blacksmiths, structural toolmakers, and units utilizing active furnaces or fire [cite: 1806, 1808].
* **South (Yāmya)**: Residential quarters for the **Vaiśyas**, transport cart drivers, merchant caravans, actors, and public dancers [cite: 1809, 1812].
* **South-West (Nairṛtī)**: Meat processing yards, shepherds, huntsmen, fishermen, and horse trainers [cite: 1813, 1815].
* **West (Vāruṇī)**: Structural carriage and chariot builders, armorers, and heavy weapons designers [cite: 1816, 1818].
* **North-West (Vāyavyā)**: Industrial laborers, supervisors, factory hands, commercial painters, and wine tavern-keepers [cite: 1823, 1825].
* **North (Uttara)**: Residential quarters of the **Brāhmaṇas**, scholars, royal astrologers, chaplains, and higher education assemblies [cite: 1828, 1849, 1851, 1852].

---

## GEOMETRIC TOWN GEOMETRY DEVIATIONS
The master layout shapes of cities carry immediate karmic consequences for the population [cite: 1725, 1727]:

| Layout Configuration | Sanskrit Term | Karmic Consequence and Fate |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Square/Rectangle** | *Caturasra* | **Auspicious**: Grants wealth, civic growth, safety, and stable governance [cite: 1422, 1425]. |
| **Truncated Corners** | *Chinna-karṇa* | Severe vulnerability to thieves, swift outbreaks of epidemics, and localized terror [cite: 1679, 1685, 1687]. |
| **Cornerless Grid** | *Vi-karṇa* | Loss of sovereignty to hostiles, systemic childlessness, and reduced lifespan [cite: 1679, 1690, 1691]. |
| **Conical / Needle Point**| *Sūci-mukha* | Total economic doom, starvation, and continuous pestilence [cite: 1679, 1695, 1697]. |
| **Circular / Globular** | *Vartula* | Total loss of financial reserves, systemic poverty, and swift death for the king [cite: 1680, 1698, 1699]. |
| **Fan-Shaped** | *Vyajana-ākṛti* | Chronic neurological diseases, storm onslaughts, and an unfaithful population [cite: 1680, 1704, 1705]. |
| **Bow-Shaped Arc** | *Cāpa-ākṛti* | Systemic breakdown of morals, marital infidelity, and empty governance [cite: 1680, 1706, 1707]. |
| **Tortuous Snake-like** | *Bhujanga-kuṭila* | Continuous attacks by elements, spirits, lightning fire, and mass deaths [cite: 1682, 1721]. |

---

## SYSTEMIC REGIONAL METRIC DEFINITIONS
Regional hierarchies are mapped strictly using urban scales and multi-village measurements [cite: 1767]:
* **Kheṭa**: An agricultural town outpost exactly **half the diameter of a Pura** [cite: 1767], situated roughly 1 *Yojana* away from a major city [cite: 1771].
* **Grāma (Village)**: A cluster of peasant houses exactly **half the diameter of a Kheṭa** [cite: 1767], separated from others by a distance of 1 *Gavyūti* (approx. 2 miles) [cite: 1772, 1795].
* **Rāṣṭra (Kingdom Domain Sizes)**:
  * **Jyeṣṭha (Large Rāṣṭra)**: Comprises between **9,064 and 9,090 functional villages** [cite: 1784, 1785].
  * **Madhyama (Middling Rāṣṭra)**: Comprises exactly **5,384 functional villages** [cite: 1786, 1788].
  * **Kaniṣṭha (Small Rāṣṭra)**: Comprises exactly **1,548 functional villages** [cite: 1790, 1791].

---

इति महाराजाधिराजश्रीभोजदेवविरचिते समराङ्गणसूत्रधारापरनाम्नि वास्तुशास्त्रे पुरनिवेशो दशमोऽध्यायः ।।१०।।
*(Thus ends the tenth chapter named Pura-niveśa in the Vāstuśāstra text, otherwise known as Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra, composed by Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva.)* [cite: 2080]

## CHAPTER 11: Vāstu-Traya-Vibhāga
### (The Division of Triad of Architectural Establishments / Siting Plans¹)

An abstract framework detailing the cardinal distribution grids of forty-five architectural deities (*Padadevatās*), configured dynamically across multi-zoned spatial footprints to map macrocosmic entities into physical ground plans [cite: 3478, 3524, 3612].

---

## THE CORE CORE MATRIX AND GRID CONFIGURATIONS

### 1. The Central Lotus Domain (The Inner Core)
The absolute center of a square boundary grid rendered into modular dimensions belongs exclusively to the primeval creator entity [cite: 3468, 3470]:
* **Brahmā**: Stationed exactly at the navel or core heart of the grid framework, occupying a vast modular sector spanning **nine squares** (*Navapada*) [cite: 3469, 3470]. He is traditionally conceptualized as a thousand-faced, omniscient entity wielding infinite, inscrutable creative potential (*Acinṭya-vibhava*) [cite: 2987, 2988].

### 2. The Internal Concentric Circle (*Antaḥ-saṁśrayā Devāḥ*)
Directly flanking the sovereign central zone of Brahmā, four dynamic primary solar and ancestral configurations govern the core structural axes, each occupying **six blocks** (*Ṣaṭpada*) [cite: 3471, 3475, 3490, 3492, 3497]:
* **Aryamā**: Dominating the Eastern axial quadrant, shifting metric alignment across six units [cite: 3471, 3473].
* **Vivasvān**: Occupying the Southern operational axis across six modular blocks [cite: 3475, 3477].
* **Mitra**: Governing the Western hydraulic alignment sector spanning six metric divisions [cite: 3490, 3510].
* **Pṛthivīdhara**: Anchoring the Northern structural stability quadrant across six fixed blocks [cite: 3492, 3511].

### 3. Intermediate Inner Corner Pairs
At the absolute junction zones where these directional axes cross inside the second layer, pairs of minor elements occupy **two blocks** each (*Padika*) [cite: 3472, 3476, 3491, 3493, 3518]:
* **South-East (Āgneyī)**: *Savitā* and *Sāvitra* [cite: 3472, 3474].
* **South-West (Nairṛtī)**: *Jaya* and *Indra* [cite: 3476, 3477].
* **North-West (Vāyavyā)**: *Yakṣmā* and *Rudra* [cite: 3490, 3491].
* **North-East (Īśānī)**: *Āpa* and *Āpavatsa* [cite: 3493].

---

## THE PERIMETER RING (*BAHIḤ-STHITĀ DEVĀḤ*)
Surrounding the internal sectors, a peripheral protective chain of **thirty-two external elements** tracks sequentially along a perfect clockwise circuit (*Pradakṣiṇam*), commencing directly at the North-East intermediate corner [cite: 3145, 3497, 3500, 3501]:

$$	ext{Īśāna} \longrightarrow 	ext{Agni} \longrightarrow 	ext{Parjanya} \longrightarrow 	ext{Jayanta} \longrightarrow 	ext{Indra} \longrightarrow 	ext{Sūrya} \longrightarrow 	ext{Satya} \longrightarrow 	ext{Bhṛśa} \longrightarrow 	ext{Antarikṣa} \dots$$

These perimeter elements are divided into structural footprint classes depending on the plan scale [cite: 3524, 3547]:
* **Dvipadādhiśas (Dual-Block Occupants)**: Elements that occupy **two full compartments** wide along the outer ring (*Jayanta, Bhṛśa, Vitatha, Bhṛṅga, Sugrīva, Śoṣa, Mukhya, and Aditi*) [cite: 3544, 3546, 3572].
* **Ekapadika Occupants**: Standard peripheral units holding exactly **one grid coordinate** box wide [cite: 3547].

---

## OUTCASTE RETRIBUTIVE CORNER DEMONESSES
Situated immediately beyond the peripheral fence lines at the extreme external tips of the four diagonal axes are the spaces of four negative entities [cite: 3525, 3527]:
1. **Carakī**: Relegated strictly to the far North-East corner extension [cite: 3526, 3538].
2. **Pūtanā**: Relegated to the far South-East corner extension [cite: 3526, 3538].
3. **Pāparākṣasī**: Relegated to the far South-West corner extension [cite: 3526, 3538].
4. **Vidārī**: Relegated to the far North-West corner extension [cite: 3526, 3538].

* **Socio-Urban Rule**: These extreme external coordinates are explicitly stripped of structural *Padabhoga* (divine spatial sharing) [cite: 3528, 3530]. They represent localized systemic imbalances, designated by classical town planners exclusively for outcaste quarters (*Śvapacas*) and sanitation elements [cite: 3536, 3537].

---

इति महाराजाधिराजश्रीभोजदेवविरचिते समराङ्गणसूत्रधारापरनाम्नि वास्तुशास्त्रे वास्तुत्रयविभागो नाम एकादशोऽध्यायः ।।
*(Thus ends the eleventh chapter named Vāstu-traya-vibhāga in the Vāstuśāstra text, otherwise known as Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra, composed by Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva.)* [cite: 3261, 3638]

---

### CHAPTER 11 FOOTNOTES & CRITICAL NOTE EXTENSIONS
1. **Grid Scale Equivalencies**: Classical text guidelines noted by commentators like Utpala outline that while square patterns remain the master templates, these coordinates extrapolate seamlessly onto triangular (*Tryasra*), hexagonal (*Ṣaḍasra*), and octagonal structures via proportional area math rules [cite: 3617, 3621].

---

## CHAPTER 12: Nādī-Vaṁśānuvaṁśa-Nirṇaya
### (The Proportional Vectors, Structural Axes, and Veins of the Site Plan)

An advanced text tracking the structural anatomy, orientation layout lines (*Vaṁśas*), diagnostic grids, and diagonal axes that run through the living structural canvas of a building site (*Vāstu-deha*) [cite: 3457, 3460].

---

## MODULAR GRID FRAMEWORKS (PADA-VIBHĀGANI)
Ancient architectural design utilizes multi-tiered metric scaling grids tailored directly to the building's programmatic typology [cite: 3130]:

### 1. Kaniṣṭha Vāstu (The Sixteen-Square Grid / Ṣoḍaśāspada)
A basic $4 	imes 4$ layout standard reserved for minor layouts or compact spaces [cite: 3266, 3268]:
* **Brahmā** anchors the four central coordinates ($4 	imes 4$ framework resolution splits) [cite: 3281, 3283].
* Primary axial anchors (*Āryamā, Vivasvān, Mitra, Kṣmādhara*) occupy exactly half a square block each [cite: 3284, 3285, 3286].
* Corner configurations drop to precise fractional distributions of one-quarter and one-eighth padic units [cite: 3288, 3292, 3293].

### 2. Catuhṣaṣṭi-Pada Vāstu (The Sixty-Four Square Grid)
An $8 	imes 8$ layout master standard specifically applied by engineers for temples (*Prāsādas*), palaces, military base camps, and cantonments [cite: 3141, 3142, 3613]. Brahmā occupies exactly four central squares here [cite: 3577].

### 3. Ekāśīti-Pada Vāstu (The Eighty-One Square Grid)
A $9 	imes 9$ layout master standard applied for the residential buildings of all societal castes, common domestic dwellings, and civil administrative town structures [cite: 2981, 3135, 3137]. Brahmā occupies the nine central grid squares [cite: 3313, 3614].

---

## THE STRUCTURAL VECTOR ANATOMY OF THE SITE PLAN
The architectural site is evaluated not as a static geometric plot, but as a dynamic structural anatomy (*Vāstu-puruṣa*) [cite: 3362, 3367]. Its directional vectors are governed by strict mathematical lines [cite: 3398]:

```
[North-West]                           [North-East] (Crest/Head)
       \                                   /
        \    [MAHĀ-VAṀŚA] (Spinal Axis)   /
         \               |               /
          \              |              /
           \             |             /
            \------------+------------/  <--- [ANUVAMŚA] (Transverse Ribs)
           /             |                       /              |                       /               |                       /                |                       /                                   [South-West]                           [South-East]
```

### 1. Mahā-Vaṁśa (The Spine Lines)
The central geometric axes mapping straight across the master plan [cite: 3403]:
* Running directly East-to-West and North-to-South through the absolute grid center [cite: 3403].
* **Metric Width**: Defined as exactly **one-fifth part of a grid unit** ($1/5 	ext{ of a Pada}$) [cite: 3405].
* **Rule**: These core axes represent the main spatial arteries. Laying heavy stone walls, columns, or timber frames directly on top of a *Mahā-Vaṁśa* is strictly prohibited [cite: 3436, 3438]. Violating this structural rule causes the collapse of the project and structural failure for the owner [cite: 3445, 3447].

### 2. Vaṁśas (The Master Diagonals)
The primary diagonal lines running from corner to corner across the square site template [cite: 1428, 3415]:
* Running directly from North-East to South-West, and from North-West to South-East [cite: 1428, 3415].
* **Metric Width**: Calculated precisely as **one-sixteenth part of a single grid unit** ($1/16 	ext{ of a Pada}$) [cite: 3402].

### 3. Anuvaṁśas (The Transverse Ribs)
The parallel secondary lines running transverse to the master diagonals, functioning structurally like parallel supporting skeletal ribs across the grid layout [cite: 3416, 3418].

### 4. Nādīs (The Intermediary Arteries)
The critical diagonal lines running parallel to the primary corners and framing the ears and sensory regions of the *Vāstu-puruṣa* anatomy [cite: 3399, 3401].

---

## DIAGNOSTIC INTERSECTION MARMAS (VULNERABLE SPOTS)
* **Marmas (Primary Vital Crossings)**: The absolute points where the primary *Vaṁśas* (diagonals) cross and intersect with one another [cite: 3417, 3419]. These points are highly sensitive to weight variations [cite: 3440].
* **Upamarmas (Secondary Crossings)**: The precise midpoints and centers of individual grid squares where transverse *Anuvaṁśas* meet [cite: 3420, 3422].
* **Metric Ratios**: The spatial vulnerability thresholds of these intersection points are mathematically calculated as fractions of a single plot footprint, spanning values of $1/8	ext{th}$, $1/10	ext{th}$, $1/12	ext{th}$, and $1/16	ext{th}$ [cite: 3421, 3423]. The $1/8	ext{th}$ fractional crossings represent the absolute maximum risk zones [cite: 3423].
* **Structural Safety Rule**: Encroaching on or loading these structural crossing points (*Marmas*) with masonry columns, heavy load-bearing frames, or doors introduces structural errors, resulting in systemic defects and project failure [cite: 3449, 3451].

---

*(Thus ends the twelfth chapter named Nādī-vaṁśānuvaṁśa-nirṇaya in the Vāstuśāstra text, otherwise known as Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra, composed by Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva.)* [cite: 3462]

## CHAPTER 13: Marma-Vedha
### (The Structural Obstructions and Protection of Vital Coordinates)

A technical text detailing *Marma-Vedha* (structural penetration or load errors over vital coordinates), outlining the defects caused by misplacing heavy architectural elements on a grid [cite: 3110, 3117].

---

## TOXIC STRUCTURAL PENETRATION (VEDHA) EFFECTS
Placing structural architectural members—such as stone pillars, masonry walls, cross-beams, or door jambs—directly over the vital crossing points (*Marmas*) or line vectors of the *Vāstu Grid* causes systemic imbalances [cite: 3172, 3192]:

* **Wall/Door Misplacement over Marmas**: Shifting load-bearing wall extensions or structural framing over a vital intersection point results in severe structural errors, long-term financial failure, and decay of the family line [cite: 3168, 3172, 3173].
* **Pillar Obstructions (*Stambha-Vedha*)**: Erecting a primary load-bearing column directly onto an active intersecting axis leads to structural hazards and failure for the property owner [cite: 3180, 3182].
* **Main Beams over Grid Lines (*Tulā-Vedha*)**: Running heavy main structural beams (*Bhāratulas*) or secondary cross-beams (*Tulopatulas*) directly aligned with the *Vaṁśa* coordinates introduces severe stress faults, traditionally causing deep distress to the family line [cite: 3180, 3182, 3196].
* **Window/Ventilator Alignment Deviations**: Cutting window frames (*Vātāyanas*) or ventilation lines directly across internal diagonal arteries (*Nādīs*) causes systemic energy imbalances, leaving the structure vulnerable to damage or theft [cite: 3189, 3212, 3213, 3401].
* **Bedstead Alignment (*Śayyā-Vedha*)**: Aligning domestic beds or master bedroom platforms directly over the primary diagonal vectors of the house grid brings illness and distress to the lineage [cite: 3208, 3210].
* **Misplaced Central Doors**: Constructing a primary entrance door precisely at the absolute geometric center of a house grid creates severe structural vulnerability, causing instability and decay for the household [cite: 3217, 3228].

---

## EXEMPTIONS FROM STRUCTURAL VEDHA DEFECTS
While load-bearing elements must never puncture or overlay these critical grid lines and intersection points, minor ornamental or lightweight functional wood structures are completely exempt [cite: 2922, 3224].

The following elements do not cause *Marma-Vedha* defects and can safely intersect grid lines in town planning, palaces, and residential houses [cite: 2927, 3224, 3229]:
* **Decorative Elements**: Ceremonial buntings, light canvas flappers, banners, or lightweight lighting fixtures [cite: 2927, 3229].
* **Lightweight Frames**: Lofty hollow bamboo poles, decorative gourds, or structural *Tumbikās* [cite: 2927, 3229, 3241].
* **Standard Crossbars**: Transverse structural latching bars or lightweight door bolts (*Indrakīlas*) [cite: 2927, 3229, 3242].

---

### Head and Sensory Organs
* **Crest / Crown of the Head**: **Agni** (*Śikhin*), the element of absolute transformative fire [cite: 2948, 2950, 3370].
* **Eyes**: Shared by **Diti** and **Parjanya** (the lord of rains/clouds) [cite: 2948, 2950, 3149].
* **Ears**: Governed by **Jayanta** and **Aditi** [cite: 2949, 2951].
* **Mouth**: Anchored by the wind element, **Vāyu** [cite: 2949, 2951].

### Upper Torso and Arms
* **Right Arm**: Occupied by five celestial markers: *Satya, Bhṛśa, Nabha, Vāyu, and Pūṣā* [cite: 2958, 2963].
* **Left Arm**: Occupied by five structural markers: *Yakṣmā, Roga, Nāga, Mukhya, and Bhallāṭa* [cite: 2957, 2962].
* **Right Shoulder Joint / Elbow**: Governed by *Savitra* and *Savitā* [cite: 2959, 2964].
* **Left Shoulder Joint / Elbow**: Governed by *Rudra* and *Śaktidhara* [cite: 2959, 2964].
* **Chest**: Balanced by *Mahendra, Caraka, and Āpavatsa* [cite: 2953, 2955].
* **Right Pap**: Anchored by *Aryamā* [cite: 2956, 2962].
* **Left Pap**: Anchored by *Pṛthivīdhara* [cite: 2956, 2962].

### Lower Torso and Core
* **Heart Area**: The absolute center belonging to the self-born **Brahmā** [cite: 2960, 2965, 3376].
* **Right Flank**: Guarded by *Vitatha* and *Gṛhakṣata* (*Okaḥkṣata*) [cite: 2961, 2965, 3012].
* **Left Flank**: Guarded by *Śoṣa* and *Asura* [cite: 2966, 2968].
* **Abdomen**: Governed by the paired solar controllers, **Mitra** and **Vivasvān** [cite: 2967, 2969].
* **Genital Organ System**: Center anchored by **Śakra** (*Indra*) and **Jayanta** [cite: 2970, 2975, 3376].

### Lower Limbs
* **Right Thigh**: Governed by **Yama** (lord of law and death) [cite: 2970, 2971, 2975].
* **Left Thigh**: Governed by **Varuṇa** (lord of structural waters) [cite: 2970, 2971, 2975].
* **Right Shank / Knee**: Guarded by *Gandharva, Bhṛṅgarijā,* and *Mṛga* [cite: 2976, 2978].
* **Left Shank / Knee**: Guarded by *Dauvārika, Sugrīva, and Puṣpadanta* [cite: 2977, 2978].
* **Soles of the Feet**: Anchored by the **Pitṛs** (the collective ancestors), resting in the South-West quadrant [cite: 2977, 2978, 3376].

## CONTEXTUAL ORIENTATION MANDATES
The physical direction of the *Vāstu-puruṣa* body changes depending on the plan scale used by the architect [cite: 3097]:
1. **In Eighty-One Square Plans ($9 	imes 9$ Grid)**: The head of the anthropomorphic figure faces directly into the **North-East** (*Īśāna*) quadrant [cite: 2979, 2981, 3370].
2. **In Sixty-Four Square Plans ($8 	imes 8$ Grid)**: The head shifts to face directly along the primary Eastern vector, **Mahendrī** (*Aindrī*) [cite: 2980, 2982, 2996].

## CHAPTER 15: Rājaniveśaḥ
### (The Siting and Architectural Planning of the Royal Palace)

An architectural text defining structural parameters for the zoning, grid allocation, and micro-building construction of a King's sovereign palace complex (*Rājaniveśa*) inside a fortified city [cite: 4928, 4929].

---

## GRID AND METRIC DIMENSIONS FOR THE REGINAL COMPLEX
The master palace layout is mapped across a **sixty-four square grid standard** (*Catuḥṣaṣṭi-pada*), carefully integrated with defensive perimeter ramparts (*Prākāra*), deep moats, wall towers, and city gates [cite: 4930, 4931, 4932].

### Location Siting
The complex must be set up slightly west of the city’s absolute grid core [cite: 4942]. It must rest on land that naturally shelves toward the north and east, or is structurally elevated to the east to guarantee administrative victory and prestige [cite: 4938, 4940].

### Tripartite Structural Scales
The overall operational size of the palace envelope drops into three modular benchmarks [cite: 4959]:
1. **Jyeṣṭha (Largest)**: Measuring exactly **two hundred Dhanus** square ($800 	imes 800 	ext{ Hastas}$ / cubits) [cite: 1431, 4959]. This scale is built exclusively inside major capital cities [cite: 4962].
2. **Madhyama (Middling)**: Measuring exactly **one hundred and sixty-two Hastas** square [cite: 4960, 4964].
3. **Kaniṣṭha (Smallest)**: Measuring exactly **one hundred and eight Hastas** square [cite: 4960, 4964].

---

### Additional Structural Siting Zones:
* **Bhallāṭa**: Standard elite location for the dairy farm and state cow pens [cite: 5096].
* **Vivasvān**: Heavy military stables for the elephant brigades and war chariots [cite: 5038, 5040].
* **Bhūdhara / Pṛthivīdhara**: Reserved for the King’s royal consecration dais, state treasury records, state fly-whisks, parasols, and the central counsel chamber [cite: 5104, 5105].
* **Jaya**: Command quarters and residential palace of the Commander-in-Chief (*Senāpati*) [cite: 5142, 5149].
* **Mukhya**: Siting for the physical fitness gymnasiums, athletic courts, theatrical music halls, and a fine picture gallery [cite: 5093, 5095].
* **Aditi**: Reserved exclusively for the residential palace of the Queen Mother, palanquin storage, and drawing rooms [cite: 5117, 5119, 5120].
* **Apa / Āpavatsa**: Open areas designated for elephant wash basins and clear lotus lakes with crane sanctuaries [cite: 5127, 5130, 5133].
* **Diti**: Residential quarters for maternal uncles, extended aunts, and royal kinsmen [cite: 5131, 5134].

## CHAPTER 16: Vana-Praveśa
### (The Harvesting of Timber and Structural Forestry Rituals¹)

A specialized text regulating the logging windows, planetary timing cycles, botanical criteria, and ritual procedures for selecting and felling timber for civil and royal architecture [cite: 4556, 4557].

---

## CHRONOLOGICAL AND ASTRONOMICAL WINDOWS
Forest entry for timber harvesting must never happen haphazardly. It is restricted to favorable planetary windows evaluated via the *Nakṣatras* (planetary positions) [cite: 4558, 4561].
* **Felling/Chiselling Actions**: Undertaken during sharp, dynamic lunar stations under the supervision of the master architect (*Sthapati*) [cite: 4585, 4587].
* **Transport Ingress**: Materials must be handled under static or mobile structural stations, moving systematically from north to east [cite: 4558, 4588].

---

## LAND AND BOTANICAL REJECTION CRITERIA
Trees growing in the following locations are fundamentally defective and strictly prohibited from structural use [cite: 4594, 4595]:
* **Prohibited Sites**: Urban cremation grounds, cemeteries, boundaries of city roads, public village paths, marshy lake edges, sacred temples, hermitages (*Āśramas*), and water reservoirs [cite: 4596, 4598].
* **Prohibited Soils**: Highly acidic, acrid, bitter, sour, alkaline, sandy, or deep trench-riddled ground [cite: 4610, 4611].
* **Unsafe Conditions**: Trees struck by lightning bolts, shattered by hurricanes, worn out with age, hollowed by pests, or broken by river torrents [cite: 4642, 4647]. Trees housing beehives, snake dens, or large owl nests are also banned [cite: 4649, 4664, 4669].

---

## TIMBER SPECIES CODIFIED BY CASTE AND APPLICATION
The selection of mature wood is carefully categorized based on structural load requirements and use [cite: 4625, 4716]:

### 1. The Four Exalted Social Classes
* **Brāhmaṇas**: *Suradāru* (Pinus Deodara / Deodar Pine), *Candana* (Sandalwood), *Śamī*, and *Madhūka* [cite: 4625, 4673, 4712].
* **Kṣatriyas**: *Aśvattha*, *Khadira* (Catechu), *Arariṣṭa*, and *Bilva* [cite: 4625, 4673].
* **Vaiśyas**: *Jīvaka*, *Sindhuka*, *Syandana*, and *Khadira* [cite: 4625, 4626, 4673].
* **Śūdras**: *Tinduka*, *Sarga*, *Arjuna*, *Amra* (Mango), and *Śāla* (Teak equivalents) [cite: 4626, 4673, 4686].

### 2. High-Strength Timber for Heavy Framing
For columns and main load-bearing arrays, the text praises *Khadira* trees, *Sarga*, *Añjana*, *Aśoka*, *Kadara*, and *Vikankaṭa* because of their proven weight tolerance and moisture resistance [cite: 4637, 4651, 4672, 4712, 4716]. Longevity testing tracks mature *Khadira* species up to a structural lifecycle of three hundred years [cite: 4616, 4637].

---

## RITUAL FELLING AND CROSS-SECTION MANDALAS

### The Midnight Expulsion Ritual
Arriving at the chosen tree, the architect performs a mandatory pacificatory ritual (*Bali*) at night using incense and food offerings [cite: 4792]. He recites an explicit warning to any hidden spirits or elementals residing within the branches [cite: 4794]:
> "The goblins and elemental beings taking refuge over this tree may get out. I shall take to the task of felling; an exit from this old coordinates must be taken." [cite: 4794, 4795]

---

### Cross-Section Defect Analysis (Cross-Section Mandalas)
When felling the tree at dawn with tools sharpened with beeswax [cite: 4811, 4813], the master craftsman must inspect the color variations visible on the freshly cut cross-section core [cite: 4863, 4866]:

| Mandala Color Profile | Internal Hidden Object Predicted | Architectural Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Madder-Dye Red (*Mañjiṣṭhā*)** | Hidden Frog locked in the sapwood [cite: 4864, 4867] | **Inauspicious**: Rejected [cite: 4893] |
| **Tawny/Copper (*Kapila*)** | Hidden Rat nested within [cite: 4864, 4867] | **Predicts Death**: Banned [cite: 4894] |
| **Dark Treacle/Molasses Shade** | Hidden Honey reservoir or pyrites [cite: 4864, 4867]| **Danger of Thieves**: Banned [cite: 4889] |
| **Bright Crimson/Aruna** | Hidden Chameleon/Lizard [cite: 4865, 4867] | **Inauspicious**: Rejected [cite: 4893] |
| **Pigeon-Gray / Ash Hue** | Hidden House Lizard [cite: 4881, 4883] | **Inauspicious**: Rejected [cite: 4893] |
| **Polished Sword / Bright Metallic**| Subterranean water column flowing directly beneath [cite: 4881, 4884]| **Auspicious**: Paves way for water foundations [cite: 4884] |

## CHAPTER 17: Śakra-Dhvajotsava-Vidhi
### (The Engineering, Mechanics, and Celebration of Indra's Royal Banner)

An entry documenting the math calculations, mechanical pulley setups (*Yantras*), scale metrics, and political state rituals for erecting *Śakra-Dhvaja* (Indra's Banner), symbolizing the victory of state order over chaotic forces [cite: 3968, 3971].

---

## DIMENSIONAL PROPORTIONS AND STRUCTURAL COMPONENTS

### Tripartite Standard Metric Scales
The length of the master standard staff (*Lakaṭa*) is built according to three dimensional benchmarks [cite: 4064, 4126]:
* **Jyeṣṭha (Premium Standard)**: Exactly **thirty-two cubits** ($32 	ext{ Hastas}$ / approx. 48 feet) [cite: 4062, 4064].
* **Madhyama (Middling Standard)**: Exactly **twenty-eight cubits** ($28 	ext{ Hastas}$) [cite: 4062, 4064].
* **Kaniṣṭha (Baseline Standard)**: Exactly **twenty-four cubits** ($24 	ext{ Hastas}$) [cite: 4064].

### Tapering Ratios
The structural breadth thickness parameters follow a strict sliding scale [cite: 4065]:
* For every single cubit of height rise, the outer diameter must taper down by precisely **half an Aṅgula** from the base dimension [cite: 4065].
* The top apex diameter must resolve to half the thickness calculated at the structural root base [cite: 4067].

---

### The Subordinate Standard Assembly (*Śakra-Kumārīs*)
The primary central staff—representing the mother post *Indra-Mātā* (or *Janitrī*) [cite: 4105, 4111]—is supported by an outer ring of five or seven smaller, auxiliary flag staffs known as the daughters (*Śakra-Kumārīs*) [cite: 4105, 4113, 4115]. These daughter posts are mathematically scaled as proportional fractions of the main height [cite: 4114, 4116]:
* *Nandā* and *Upanandā*: Scaled to exactly three-quarters and one-half the height of the main staff respectively [cite: 4114, 4116].
* *Jayā*, *Vijayā*, and the two *Vasundharās*: Taller than the initial pair by precise sixteenth fractions ($1/16$) [cite: 4117].

---

## THE MECHANICAL ROTATING PULLEY BASE (*BHRAMA-PĪṬHA*)
The entire multi-tiered timber standard assembly is stepped into a heavy, square, load-bearing mechanical base known as the revolving fulcrum frame (*Bhrama-Pīṭha*) [cite: 4075, 4124].

```
                ||  [INDRA-MĀTĀ] (Main Standard Staff)
                ||
         =======||=======  <--- [ŚAKRA-PITAKA] (Wicker Ornaments Layer)
         |  ||  ||  ||  |
         |  ||  ||  ||  |  <--- [ŚAKRA-KUMĀRĪS] (Daughter Standard Rings)
         ===============
                ||
                ||
         [======||======]  <--- [AKṢA] (Heavy Dual Structural Axles)
         |  [VEDHA]    |  <--- Mortised Depth Perforations [cite: 4080]
         |              |
    ==========================
    [BHRAMA-PĪṬHA] BASE FRAME  <--- Heavy Rammed Structural Platform [cite: 4075]
```

* **Axial Connection**: The unit is cross-locked by two heavy structural poles (*Akṣas*), extending into precision-bored mortised sockets (*Vedha*) inside the revolving base frame [cite: 4079, 4080]. This enables smooth vertical lever actions during the initial lift [cite: 4081].
* **Rigid Bracing**: The outer frame is clamped tightly with high-tensile iron brackets and heavy pins to maintain equilibrium during strong gales [cite: 4222, 4225].
* **Guy Lines**: Eight heavy structural guide ropes (*Rajjus*)—representing the eight protective agencies of state order—are tightly braided to a diameter of one-sixth the pole thickness [cite: 4380, 4382]. Each rope must measure exactly three times the total banner length to ensure solid grounding [cite: 4381, 4382].

---

## THE RITUAL LITURGY & CELEBRATION
On the auspicious first day of the bright fortnight of the monsoon month of *Āśvin*, under clear planetary positions [cite: 4153, 4155], the entire civil population gathers [cite: 4156].

The staff is washed in medicinal herbal infusions, anointed with fresh clarified butter, and placed horizontally across two carved supporting wooden structures shaped like female elephants (*Dāru-hastinīs*) [cite: 4159, 4161, 4164].

### The Raising Liturgy
While bards, dancers, and braying trumpets fill the air with sound, the master architect steps forward to the base [cite: 4252, 4265]. Holding hands folded, he mutters the mandatory cosmic lifting chant [cite: 4532, 4533]:
> *"Om Namo Bhagavati Vāgule Sarva-Viṭa-Pramardani Svāhā!* > As you stood victorious during the ancient battles between the gods and the demons, likewise, Oh Lord of Gods! Arise and stand tall, adored by us, to grant absolute triumph to our king!" [cite: 4534, 4536, 4537, 4538]

Using the guy lines and mechanical levers, the crowd raises the staff into a perfect vertical position [cite: 4541, 4546]. To mark the occasion, the king must declare an absolute amnesty for all prisoners across the kingdom for ten days and strictly ban animal slaughter [cite: 4516, 4518].

---

## INAUSPICIOUS BREAKAGE OMENS AND FATES
Any technical or mechanical accident during the lifting or lowering process carries critical warning signs for the kingdom [cite: 4031, 4034]:
* **Leftward Twist**: If the staff skews or twists leftward during its connection, it predicts structural danger for the chief architect [cite: 4321, 4322].
* **Base Collapse / Fall**: If the pole slips its brackets and crashes to the bare ground, it foretells the immediate dethronement and fall of the reigning king [cite: 4312, 4313, 4314].
* **Splitting / Splintering**: Structural fracture or splitting on the outer wood panels indicates the death of the Queen or internal political disasters [cite: 4329, 4331].

## CHAPTER 18: Vāstu-Nāma-Nighaṇṭu
### (The Comprehensive Lexicon of Settlement Types and Architectural Components)

An architectural dictionary defining the precise terminology for settlement scales, building typologies, and functional components used by structural engineers [cite: 3658, 3806].

---

## REGIONAL TYPOLOGIES AND SETTLEMENT SCALES
* **Pura / Nagara**: A fortified urban capital complete with continuous masonry defense walls, perimeter moats, and major civic highway layouts [cite: 1413, 1419, 3667].
* **Karvaṭa / Kharvaṭa**: A mid-scale secondary market town or regional hub measuring half the size of a standard city [cite: 1436, 3654, 3668].
* **Nigama**: A bustling commercial trading center or town populated mostly by wandering merchant guilds and trading caravans [cite: 3671, 3675].
* **Pattana**: A highly specialized port city, coastal trading center, or river-mouth trading hub layout (*Puṭabhedana*) filled with merchant ships and customs offices [cite: 3660, 3663, 3673, 3679].
* **Grāma**: A common agricultural village or localized cluster of rustic family houses layout [cite: 3655, 3658, 3669].
* **Goṣṭha / Gokula**: A specialized rural hamlet or secure cow-pen settlement custom-built for herding kine [cite: 3656, 3659].
* **Pallī / Pallikā**: A tiny, isolated hillside hamlet or settlement constructed of wild grass huts and mud walls, inhabited mostly by wild tribes or foresters (*Pulindas*) [cite: 3665, 3666].
* **Janapada**: The collective term for all rural countryside lands, agricultural sectors, and provincial districts surrounding a fortified city [cite: 3667, 3692].

---

## SYNONYMS OF THE HOUSE OR ABODE
To clarify structural descriptions, the text identifies a common set of interchangeable terms used for a dwelling place or building [cite: 3694, 3696]:
> **Āvāsa • Sadana • Sadma • Niketa • Mandira • Saṁsthāna • Nidhana • Dhiṣṇya • Bhavana • Vasati • Kṣaya • Agāra • Saṁśraya • Nīḍa • Geha • Śaraṇa • Ālaya • Nilaya • Layana • Veśma • Gṛha • Okaḥ • Pratiśraya** [cite: 3694, 3695, 3696]

---

## STRUCTURAL PARTS OF A BUILDING DEFINED

### 1. Vertical Circulation and Upper Levels
* **Harmya**: The open upper roof, upper terrace, or top-most habitable level of a palace or masonry mansion [cite: 3697, 3698].
* **Sopāna**: A wide, permanent, stone-paved structural staircase or flight of steps [cite: 3697, 3698].
* **Niḥśreṇi**: A lightweight, movable ladder built by fastening wooden rungs or cross-sticks between two upright poles [cite: 3699, 3701].
* **Saudha**: A high mansion or palace completely covered in smooth, polished lime-stucco plaster [cite: 3702, 3703].
* **Kuṭṭima**: A solid, decorated mosaic floor or stone-paved interior courtyard [cite: 3702, 3703].

### 2. Windows, Air Shafts, and Projections
* **Vātāyana**: A primary window opening cut into load-bearing walls to provide light and airflow [cite: 3716, 3718].
* **Avalokanaka**: A minor ventilation lattice, shuttered window, or small viewport aperture [cite: 3717, 3718].
* **Uloka**: A central skylight opening or direct vertical air shaft cut into the roof of a house [cite: 3719, 3721].
* **Niryūha / Mattavāraṇaka**: A projecting timber bracket, corbel, or structural overhang throwing out above columns or main gates [cite: 3725, 3731, 3737].
* **Valīka**: The eaves or structural edge framework of a thatched roof protruding from a wall cutout [cite: 3726, 3737].

### 3. Interior Zoning Spaces
* **Apavaraka**: A small, private, four-walled interior room—often used as a secure bedroom or private lying-in chamber [cite: 3771, 3773].
* **Śuddhānta**: The highly secure, private inner harem or women's quarters of a palace complex [cite: 3772, 3773].
* **Mahānasa**: The dedicated domestic kitchen complex or culinary hall designed for food preparation [cite: 3781, 3783].
* **Garbhagṛha**: A heavily covered, secure sanctuary room located deep within the center of a complex [cite: 3747, 3749].
* **Bhavanājīra**: The central square or open inner quadrangle court around which a house is framed [cite: 3796, 3798].
* **Dehalī**: The low structural threshold stone or horizontal block set directly beneath the doorframe entryway [cite: 3800, 3802].
* **Udakabhrama**: A functional stone drain, water outlet channel, or waste percolation conduit system [cite: 3793, 3795].

---

## THE STRUCTURAL ENCLOSURE TAXONOMY (*ŚĀLĀ TYPES*)
Residential floor plans are classified according to the number of individual wings (*Śālās*) enclosing the central courtyard [cite: 3738, 3746]:
* **Catuḥ-śāla**: A complete four-winged mansion or quadrangle house enclosing an inner open space on all four sides [cite: 3738, 3740].
* **Tri-śāla**: A three-winged configuration leaving one side open [cite: 3739, 3741].
* **Dvi-śāla**: A two-winged structural layout [cite: 3739, 3741].
* **Eka-śāla**: A single standalone structure or linear hall unit [cite: 3742, 3745].

---

## GATEWAYS AND ADVANCED FEATURES

### Toraṇa (The Ornamental Arch)
An elevated, decorative gateway built near the main portals or temple entries [cite: 3826, 3847]. It consists of two upright columns joined at the top by curved cross-beams displaying layered semi-circular patterns (*Ardha-candra*) and star or disk markers (*Thakāra*) at the structural joints [cite: 3829, 3831, 3834, 3853].

### Dhārāgāra (The Automated Fountain House)
An architectural luxury chamber engineered with a complex network of hidden internal copper and wooden pipes (*Kaṣṭhanālas*) running behind the walls and ceilings [cite: 3883, 3891]. Water is forced under pressure through small apertures carved into the nostrils, eyes, and mouths of stone animal figures—such as lions, bulls, and monkeys—creating a continuous shower system inside the room [cite: 3886, 3889, 3892].

### (The Modular Combinations and Permutations of Four-Winged Houses)

An exhaustive mathematical and taxonomic treatise detailing the architectural layouts, naming structures, and vent positioning rules (*Mūṣās*) for residential four-winged quadrangle complexes (*Catuḥśālas*) [cite: 6187, 6203].

The text codifies structural models categorized systematically by the raw quantity of built wings (*Śālās*) integrated around central inner courtyards [cite: 6191, 6225]:

* **Tri-śāla (3-Winged)**: 72 standard modular configurations [cite: 1412, 6192, 6193].
* **Catuḥ-śāla (4-Winged)**: 256 mathematically standard permutations [cite: 6194, 6196].
* **Pañca-śāla (5-Winged)**: 1,025 dynamic layout variations [cite: 6197, 6199].

## SPATIAL ANALYSIS METRICS BY GENERAL SOCIAL CLASS (*VARṆAS*)
The physical breadth limits for establishing four-winged structures are rigorously zoned based on the owner's legal caste stature [cite: 6243, 6304]:
* **Royal Generals (*Senāpatis*) & State Chaplains (*Purodhitas*)**: Broadest configurations mapping to **sixty-four cubits** ($64 	ext{ Hastas}$) [cite: 6245, 6246, 6253].
* **The Four Common Varṇas**: Sizing drops from 32, to 28, 24, 20, down to a base width of 16 cubits for the minor domestic tracks [cite: 6244, 6284, 6308].
* **Length Suffix Multipliers**: Length metrics are scaled dynamically relative to the core structural width footprints [cite: 6300, 6302]:
  * **Brāhmaṇas**: Length exceeds breadth by exactly **one-tenth part** ($+1/10$) [cite: 6298, 6302].
  * **Kṣatriyas**: Length exceeds breadth by exactly **one-eighth part** ($+1/8$) [cite: 6299, 6302].
  * **Vaiśyas**: Length exceeds breadth by exactly **one-sixth part** ($+1/6$) [cite: 6299, 6302].
  * **Śūdras**: Length exceeds breadth by exactly **one-fourth part** ($+1/4$) [cite: 6301, 6302].

## THE CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM OF CORES (*BHADRA* SYSTEMS)
Four-winged quadrangle layouts are sub-classified across extensive list groups matching the configuration of their decorative projections or layout openings (*Bhadras*) [cite: 6414, 6424]. These follow clean numeric permutations tracking active vent placement layouts (*Mūṣās*):

### 1. Eka-bhadra Configurations (8 Master Variants)
Layout options optimized via single structural projections across the main axes [cite: 6424, 6445]:

Double projection frameworks configured symmetrically along boundary grids [cite: 6447, 6454]:

### 3. Tri-bhadra, Catur-bhadra, & Pañca-bhadra Clusters

* **Pañca-bhadra (56 Options)**: High-order systems tracking precise fivefold balanced openings (*Kānala, Lolupa, Jihma, Prāgala, Śālina, Jinam*) [cite: 6494, 6495, 6513].
* **Ṣaḍ-bhadra, Sapta-bhadra, & Sarvatobhadra**: Culminates inside the sovereign **Sarvatobhadraka** structural layout template—built using exactly **eight identical functional openings** to guarantee perfect multi-axial protection [cite: 6513, 6524, 6526].

## CHAPTER 20: Alinda-Phala-Vidhāna
### (The Structural Placement of Verandahs and Balconies)

A diagnostic textbook tracing the architectural rules, spatial definitions, and long-term effects of placing open verandahs, porches, and balconies (*Alindas*) across residential ground plans [cite: 5427, 6028].

---

## THE LAWS OF ORIENTATION PLACEMENT (*AGRATAḤ & PṚṢṬHATAḤ*)
In standard classical architecture, orientation zones are never relative; they are governed by absolute structural entry benchmarks [cite: 6030, 6032]:
* **Agrataḥ (The Front / Agra)**: The absolute quadrant where the primary entry door is constructed [cite: 6034].
* **Pṛṣṭhataḥ (The Rear / Pṛṣṭha)**: The absolute quadrant directly opposite the primary entryway [cite: 6031, 6034].

---

## DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA FOR VERANDAH SITING (*ALINDA-PHALA*)
Constructing a single open porch, verandah, or balcony (*Eka-alinda*) requires alignment across favorable axes to prevent systemic structural imbalances [cite: 6066, 6068]:

| Balcony Axis | Sanskrit Typology | Structural and Governance Outcomes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Absolute Front** | *Agra-Alinda* | **Highly Auspicious**: Grants royal favor, state clearance, and social prestige [cite: 6069, 6107]. |
| **Right Side** | *Dakṣiṇa-Alinda* | **Highly Auspicious**: Wealth-augmenting; continuously expands private capital reserves [cite: 6069, 6106]. |
| **Left Side** | *Vāma-Alinda* | **Inauspicious / Prohibited**: Causes economic depletion and continuous structural costs [cite: 6079, 6107]. |
| **Absolute Rear** | *Pṛṣṭha-Alinda* | **Highly Dangerous**: Predicts critical illnesses or structural failure for the household master [cite: 6079, 6081, 6106]. |

---

### Dual-Axis Verandah Rules (*Dvi-Alinda*)
* **Flank Symmetrical Setup**: Having two parallel verandahs constructed on both side flanks guarantees steady influxes of capital for the family [cite: 6082, 6084].
* **Front-and-Rear Balance**: Verandahs balanced on both the front and rear axes expand agricultural grain stocks, generate structural longevity, and maintain general prosperity [cite: 6085, 6087].

---

## THE SYNTAX OF "HALAKA" WRAPAROUND BALCONIES
An *Halaka-Alinda* represents an L-shaped or combined structural wraparound balcony framework passing across adjacent quadrants [cite: 6088, 6091]:
* **Front-and-Right Wraparound**: Excellent setup; maximizes state favor and steadily augments private reserves [cite: 6089, 6090].
* **Right-and-Rear Wraparound**: Highly praised; generates elite prosperity and familial security [cite: 6095, 6096].
* **Left-and-Front / Rear-and-Left**: Strictly banned; triggers critical domestic strifes, loss of spouse, or severe state penalties [cite: 6092, 6093, 6098].

---

## THE PROHIBITION OF INTEGRATED INTERIORS (* गृहसङ्घट्ट / SAṀGHAṬṬA*)
* **Saṁghaṭta Matrix Rule**: Constructing two distinct operational rooms or halls sharing a single central wall partition without adequate modular spacing is defined as *Saṁghaṭṭa* [cite: 5423, 5425]. Architectural masters strictly forbid this layout shortcut, as it triggers physical deformities, legal entanglements, and early deaths for the occupants [cite: 5424, 5426].

---

## CHAPTER 21: Dvāsaptati-Triśāla-Lakṣaṇam
### (The Structural Metrics of the Seventy-Two Three-Winged Houses)

A technical blueprint tracing the layouts, modular variants, and specific names of the **seventy-two distinct configurations of three-winged houses** (*Triśālas*) [cite: 5435, 5436].

---

## THE FOUR RECOGNIZED MASTER ARCHETYPES
All seventy-two sub-variants are mathematically derived from four foundational archetypes, defined strictly by which directional wing (*Śālā*) is purposefully left absent from the quadrangle axis [cite: 5440, 5442]:

```
    1. HIRANYANĀBHA (Auspicious)            2. SUKṢETRA (Auspicious)
         [NORTH WING ABSENT]                    [EAST WING ABSENT]
               ======                                 ======
               |    |                                 |    |
        =======[    ]=======                   =======[    ]
        |    |        |    |                   |    |
        ====================                   ====================
        [SOUTH]      [EAST]                    [SOUTH]      [WEST]

    3. CULLĪ (Inauspicious/Banned)          4. PAKṢAGHNA (Inauspicious/Banned)
         [SOUTH WING ABSENT]                    [WEST WING ABSENT]
        ====================                          ======
        |    |        |    |                          |    |
        =======[    ]=======                   =======[    ]=======
               |    |                                 |    |        |    |
               ======                                 ====================
        [NORTH]      [EAST]                           [NORTH]      [EAST]
```

1. **Hiranyanābha**: Formed by purposefully omitting the **Northern wing** ($Uttaera	ext{-}\acute{s}\bar{a}l\bar{a}	ext{-}h\bar{i}na$) [cite: 5443, 5449]. **Highly Auspicious**: Infuses the household with continuous flow of wealth and material abundance [cite: 5451, 5452].
2. **Sukṣetra**: Formed by omitting the **Eastern wing** ($P\bar{u}rva	ext{-}\acute{s}\bar{a}l\bar{a}	ext{-}h\bar{i}na$) [cite: 5443, 5450]. **Highly Auspicious**: Enhances general prosperity and steady social growth [cite: 5453, 5454].
3. **Cullī**: Formed by omitting the **Southern wing** ($Dakṣiṇa	ext{-}\acute{s}\bar{a}l\bar{a}	ext{-}h\bar{i}na$) [cite: 5455]. **Inauspicious / Banned**: Systematically drains internal monetary reserves, ending in financial destruction [cite: 5455, 5456].
4. **Pakṣaghna**: Formed by omitting the **Western wing** ($Pa\acute{s}cima	ext{-}\acute{s}\bar{a}l\bar{a}	ext{-}h\bar{i}na$) [cite: 5457, 5460]. **Inauspicious / Banned**: Creates permanent social hostility, litigation, and early decay of children [cite: 5460].

---

## THE MODULE PERMUTATIONS (18 COMPONENT VARIANTS EACH)
By altering the internal configuration of air-vents (*Mūṣās*) and verandah extensions across the remaining wings, each of the four categories produces exactly **eighteen custom sub-types**, generating $4 	imes 18 = 72$ total designs [cite: 5461, 5485]:

### 1. Hiranyanābha Sub-Permutations (18 Options)
> **Jāmbūnada • Hiraṇya • Rukma • Hema • Kanaka • Kāñcana • Svarṇa • Suvarṇa • Santāpa • Sāra • Cāmīkara • Tapana • Tāpanīya • Śātakumbha • Hiranyanābha • Kalyāṇa • Bhūṣaṇa • Bhūtabhūṣaṇa** [cite: 5462, 5463, 5464]

### 2. Sukṣetra Sub-Permutations (18 Options)
> **Nāga • Sūryaprabha • Mattavāraṇa • Kesarī • Vāsava • Indra • Hari • Haṁsa • Sārasa • Kuñjara • Toyada • Meghamāla • Dhārāsāra • Mahodara • Kardama • Sukṣetra • Prakara • Dhānyapūraka** [cite: 5465, 5472, 5477, 5481]

### 3. Cullī Sub-Permutations (18 Options)
> **Bhujangama • Nirjīva • Vihangama • Nakula • Pannaga • Śatacchidra • Sarpa • Kopa • Bhagandara • Udvejana • Sannyāsa • Nistoya • Karuṇānana • Vāraṇa • Dāraṇa • Cullī • Kakuda • Kandara** [cite: 5484, 5485, 5489, 5491, 5492]

### 4. Pakṣaghna Sub-Permutations (18 Options)
> **Rākṣasa • Dhvāntasaṁghāta • Devārī • Suradāruṇa • Ghoṣaṇa • Vyāghra • Śārdūla • Ṣoṣaṇa • Viṣoṣaṇa • Mattada • Nīrānanda • Śākuna • Vighna • Nirghṛṇa • Ripusaṁhāra • Pakṣaghna • Sutaghna • Vairipūraṇa** [cite: 5497, 5507, 5508, 5509, 5510]

## GENERAL VENT POSITIONING STANDARD RULE
* **The Siting Mandate**: In three-winged houses, the initial four primary layout air-vents (*Mūṣās*) must always be engineered exclusively over the **outer wall perimeters**; cutting vents into the delicate inside courtyard partition walls is forbidden [cite: 5179, 5683, 5686].

## CHAPTER 22: Dviśāla-Gṛha-Lakṣaṇam
### (The Structural Metrics of the Fifty-Two Two-Winged Houses)

An operational blueprint detailing the structural zoning rules, air-vent orientations, and diagnostic definitions governing the **fifty-two distinct configurations of two-winged houses** (*Dviśālas*) [cite: 5192, 5193].

---

## THE SIX EXALTED MASTER CORE ARCHETYPES
All fifty-two sub-variants are mapped systematically across six foundational configurations of dual perpendicular or parallel wing frames [cite: 5198, 5705]:

1. **Siddhārtha**: Built by running built wings strictly along the **South and West** boundaries [cite: 6157]. **Highly Auspicious**: Functions as a catalyst for generating continuous wealth and luxury [cite: 5220, 6158].
2. **Yamasūrya**: Built by running built wings along the **North and West** boundaries [cite: 6158]. **Highly Dangerous**: Triggers severe accidental hazards and introduces the constant threat of early mortality [cite: 5223, 6159].
3. **Danda**: Built by running built wings along the **North and East** boundaries [cite: 6159]. **Inauspicious**: Brings the persistent danger of state fines, penal actions, and central punishments [cite: 5224, 6159].
4. **Vāta**: Built by running built wings along the **East and South** boundaries [cite: 6160]. **Inauspicious**: Fills the house with endless domestic quarrels, legal friction, and psychological anxiety [cite: 5226, 6161].
5. **Cullī**: Parallel wings configured to face each other directly across the **East and West** axis [cite: 6166]. **Prohibited**: Causes absolute financial depletion and regular asset losses [cite: 5227, 6167].
6. **Kāca**: Parallel wings configured to face each other across the **North and South** axis [cite: 6162]. **Prohibited**: Generates severe internal family splits and hostility among kinsmen [cite: 5233, 6165].

---

## TAXONOMIC MATRIX OF SYSTEMIC DESIGN CODES
By systematically adjusting the combinations of the internal vents (*Mūṣās*) across the boundary grids, the core lines expand into 52 precise layout designs [cite: 5200, 5275]:

### 1. The 11 Auspicious Siddhārtha Variations
> **Vasudhāra • Siddhārthaka • Kalyāṇaka • Śāśvata • Śiva • Kāmaprada • Strīda • Śānta • Niṣkalaṅka • Dhanādhiśa • Kuberaka** [cite: 5245, 5248, 5249]

### 2. The 11 Hostile Yamasūrya Variations
> **Saṁhāra • Yamasūrya • Kāla • Vaivasvata • Yama • Karāla • Vikarāla • Kabandha • Mṛtaka • Śava • Mahiṣa** [cite: 5251, 5252, 5253, 5254, 5259]

### 3. The 11 Punitive Danda Variations
> **Pracaṇḍa • Caṇḍa • Daṇḍa • Uddaṇḍa • Kāṇḍa • Koṭara • Vigraha • Nigraha • Dhūmra • Nirdhūma • Dantidāruṇa** [cite: 5262, 5263, 5264]

### 4. The 11 Volatile Vāta Variations
> **Marut • Pavana • Vāta • Anila • Prabhañjana • Ghanāri • Ambudavidhvaṁsi • Pralaya • Kalaha • Kali • Kalicullī** [cite: 5266, 5267, 5268, 5270]

### 5. Parallel Core Sub-Types (Cullī & Kāca Frameworks)
* **Cullī Permutations (4 Options)**: *Roga, Cullī, Anala, and Bhasma* [cite: 5272].
* **Kāca Permutations (4 Options)**: *Chala, Kāca, Kulaghna (or Kulaha), and Virodhi* [cite: 5273, 5274].

## AIR-VENT INTEGRATION DIRECTIVE RULE
* **The Structural Safety Rule**: In two-winged houses, cutting either a single solitary air-vent (*Mūṣā*) or dropping vents completely (*Amūṣā*) is strictly forbidden by standard engineering manuals [cite: 5232, 5234]. Every dual-winged structure must balance internal airflow via multi-vent pairings to avoid structural stress and domestic misfortune [cite: 5242].

## CHAPTER 24: Dvāra-Pīṭha-Bhitti-Māna-Vidhāna
### (The Structural Dimensions of Gates, Plinths, Walls, and Timber Joinery)

A comprehensive engineering manual recording the absolute proportional math formulas required for scaling doors, structural wall thickness parameters, masonry pedestals, and specialized single-wing configurations (*Halakas*) [cite: 7648, 7650, 8289].

---

## MASONRY AND PERIMETER PROPORTIONAL METRICS

### 1. Structural Wall Thickness Scaling Rules
The horizontal structural thickness metric of a load-bearing partition wall (*Bhitti-Vistāra*) is calculated directly as a fixed geometric fraction of the main room hall length (*Śālā*) [cite: 8385]:

$$	ext{Wall Thickness} = \frac{1}{4} 	imes 	ext{Śālā Width}$$

This structural dimension is rigorously maintained across five master scales starting at a base width of sixteen cubits ($16 	ext{ Hastas}$), modifying dimensions contextually to bypass and shield critical grid intersections (*Marmas*) from stress vectors [cite: 8318, 8321, 8386, 8389, 8390].

### 2. Pedestals, Plinths, and Door Framing
* **The Foundation Plinth (*Pīṭha*)**: Erected completely flat over smoothed subsoil, scaled exactly to half the vertical elevation height of the baseline ground level storey (*Tala*) [cite: 8403, 8406, 8424].
* **The Main Door Frame Height**: Derived proportionally by taking the total building width metrics in cubits, applying a baseline addition constant of seventy ($+70$), and dividing to optimize clearance profiles across the five master classes [cite: 8354, 8410, 8411, 8413].
* **The Frame Breadth**: Scaled mathematically to exactly **half the calculated door height**, minus a precise one-eighth fractional subtraction ($1/8$) to ensure elegant entry lines [cite: 8414, 8416].

---

## THE FIFTEEN HOLY WRAPAROUND DESIGN STYLES (*HALAKAS*)
The text records fifteen specialized structural layout designs featuring inner un-blocked masonry courtyard spaces flanked on the outside by complex corner wings, titled *Halas* (or *Halakas*) [cite: 8291, 8292, 8297].

### The Four Cardinal Auspicious Siting Templates
* **Bhadra**: Facing **East**, door set over the *Mahendra* grid coordinate, featuring an *Hastinī* room wing [cite: 8450, 8452]. **Highly Auspicious**: Maximizes structural longevity, expands royal honors, and guarantees long-term project success [cite: 8453, 8455].
* **Nandapīṭha**: Facing **South**, door set over the *Gṛhakṣata* coordinate, featuring a *Mahiṣī* room wing [cite: 8459, 8460]. **Highly Auspicious**: Fills the domestic household with continuous joy, wealth, and agricultural grain expansions [cite: 8463, 8465].
* **Saurabha**: Facing **West**, door set over the *Kusuma* coordinate, featuring a *Gāvī* room wing [cite: 8466, 8468]. **Highly Auspicious**: Optimizes agricultural commercial returns, trade velocity, and child obedience [cite: 8469, 8472].
* **Puṣkara**: Facing **North**, door set over the *Bhallāṭa* coordinate, featuring a *Chāgalī* room wing [cite: 8473, 8474, 8475]. **Highly Auspicious**: Endows the family master with absolute contentment, multi-child success, and profound social wealth [cite: 8476, 4878].

---

### Inauspicious Siting Configurations (To Be Evaded)
* **Roga**: Formed by forcing the *Halaka* to align into the North-West (*Vāyavya*) intermediate corner, accelerating physical illnesses and family decline [cite: 8305, 8325].
* **Pāpa**: Formed by misaligning vectors over North-West and Southern coordinates, bringing severe diagnostic errors and bad metrics [cite: 8328, 8331].
* **Dhvāṅkṣa**: Custom-built using inverted profiles focused into the North-East (*Īśāna*) quadrant, driving the household into critical penury and loose asset management [cite: 8316, 8339, 8341].
* **Vikṛta**: Misconfigured layout ratios that structurally isolate the main rooms, forcing the owner into early civic exile or property loss [cite: 8347, 8348].

## CHAPTER 26: Āya-Vyaya-Lakṣaṇam
### (The Mathematics of Fiscal Income, Expenditure, and Astrological Siting)

An advanced text tracking the financial forecasting calculations (*Āya-Vyaya*), seasonal felling calendars, lunar dates (*Tithis*), and mathematical formulas to determine site profitability [cite: 7278, 7335].

---

## THE CALENDAR WINDOW FOR GROUND BREAKING (*SŪTRAPĀTA*)
Applying the structural measuring line (*Sūtrapāta-Vidhi*) over the top soil must happen exclusively inside a bright fortnight (*Śukla-pakṣa*) on an astrologically cleared day [cite: 7279, 7281, 7311].

### Seasonal Month Outcomes
* **Vaiśākha (May-June)**: **Highly Auspicious**: Infuses the landlord with continuous capital and riches [cite: 7282, 7284].
* **Śrāvaṇa (August-September)**: **Highly Auspicious**: Maximizes the rapid augmentation of wealth and assets [cite: 7286].
* **Mārgaśīrṣa (December-January)**: **Highly Auspicious**: Delivers exceptional monetary gains and financial clearance [cite: 7290, 2243].
* **Sahasya / Pauṣa (January-February)**: **Auspicious**: Expands life enjoyments, comforts, and domestic desires (*Kāma*) [cite: 2243, 7290, 7299].
* **Phālguna (March-April)**: **Highly Auspicious**: Endows the structure with unprecedented prosperity and luxury (*Śrī*) [cite: 7291, 7300].

---

### Prohibited Months (To Be Avoided)
* *Caitra*: Plunges the master landlord into persistent grief and emotional distress [cite: 7282, 7284].
* *Jyeṣṭha*: High-risk window predicting early mortality for the householder [cite: 7283, 7285].
* *Āṣāḍha (Śucau)*: Destroys livestock and causes the quick decline of agricultural cattle [cite: 7283, 7285].
* *Bhadrapada (Nabhasya)*: The house owner will suffer displacement and fail to live in the home [cite: 7286, 7288].
* *Āśvin*: Triggers heavy litigation, localized disputes, and continuous social friction [cite: 7287, 7289].
* *Kārtika*: Causes the abandonment or loss of key laborers, servants, and subordinates [cite: 7287, 7289].
* *Māgha*: Carries severe physical risk from electrical storms or sudden fire destruction [cite: 7291, 7301].

### Approved Lunar Tithis (Dates)
Structural work is favored on the following lunar days: **Dvitiyā (2nd), Pañcamī (5th), Saptamī (7th), Navamī (9th), Ekādaśī (11th), and Trayodaśī (13th)** [cite: 7301, 7303].

---

## SOLAR ORIENTATION SYNC TO THE ZODIAC
To build a door facing a specific cardinal direction, the position of the Sun across the twelve signs of the zodiac must align precisely to avoid creating an empty structural void (*Śūnya*) [cite: 7312, 7314, 7316]:

* **West-Facing Entries (*Varuṇa-Dik*)**: Authorized only when the Sun resides inside **Kanyā** (Virgo), **Tulā** (Libra), or **Vṛścika** (Scorpio) [cite: 7312, 7313].
* **South-Facing Entries**: Strictly forbidden if the Sun resides in **Kumbha** (Aquarius), **Makara** (Capricorn), or **Dhanus** (Sagittarius), as it brings state penalties [cite: 7315, 7317, 7324, 7325].
* **East-Facing Entries**: Forbidden if the Sun resides inside **Mīna** (Pisces), **Vṛṣabha** (Taurus), or **Meṣa** (Aries), to prevent asset raids by thieves or rulers [cite: 7326, 7328, 7329, 7333].
* **North-Facing Entries**: Forbidden if the Sun resides in **Mithuna** (Gemini), **Siṁha** (Leo), or **Karka** (Cancer), as it triggers serfdom and poverty [cite: 7330, 7334].

---

## THE CORE MATHEMATICAL REVENUE FRACTIONS (*ĀYA*)
To map out the financial blueprint, the total length metric of the site is multiplied by its width in cubits [cite: 7361, 7363]. The resulting total area superficial contents (*Kṣetraphala*) are then divided using an absolute modulus divider of eight ($/8$) [cite: 7361, 7363, 7445].

$$	ext{Āya Formula Remainder} = \frac{	ext{Length} 	imes 	ext{Width}}{8}$$

The remaining integer value ($0 	ext{ through } 7$) indicates the corresponding *Āya* index, tracking the long-term cash flow profile of the property [cite: 7364, 7445]:

| Remainder Index | Sanskrit Term | Symbolized Entity Profile | Financial Siting Outcome |
| :---: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | **Dhvaja** | The Standard / Flag [cite: 7364, 7366] | **Highly Auspicious**: Expands revenue gains across all classes [cite: 7382, 7390]. |
| **2** | **Dhūma** | The Smoke / Cloud [cite: 7365, 7366] | *Inauspicious*: Creates internal family stress and friction [cite: 7382, 7384]. |
| **3** | **Siṁha** | The Sovereign Lion [cite: 7365, 7366] | **Highly Auspicious**: Delivers absolute victory, best for Brāhmaṇas [cite: 7382, 7391]. |
| **4** | **Śvā** | The Wild Dog [cite: 7365, 7366] | *Dangerous*: Triggers endless lawsuits and bitter conflicts [cite: 7383, 7384]. |
| **5** | **Vṛṣabha** | The Sacred Bull [cite: 7365, 7366] | **Highly Auspicious**: Wealth, grain storage expansions, best for Vaiśyas [cite: 7383, 7393]. |
| **6** | **Khara** | The Pack Donkey [cite: 7366] | *Dangerous*: Characterized by spouse distress and manual labor [cite: 7383, 7385]. |
| **7** | **Gaja** | The Royal Tusker Elephant [cite: 7366]| **Highly Auspicious**: Grants safety, stability, best for Kṣatriyas [cite: 7386, 7393]. |
| **0 / 8** | **Dhvāṅkṣa** | The Carrion Crow [cite: 7367, 7377] | *Fatal*: Strictly banned; brings early death to the owner [cite: 7386, 7388]. |

### The Golden Rule of Siting Balances
A building layout is considered pristine and mathematically balanced only when its computed operational income metric (*Āya*) structurally exceeds its calculated operational expenditures (*Vyaya*) [cite: 7503, 7507, 7514]. Properties displaying identical or reversed revenue-to-cost balances are unsafe and must be abandoned [cite: 7514, 7516].

दक्षिण दिकस्य काष्ठमूलं क्षिपेत्। तस्पाग्रे पादान्तभागस्य काष्ठमूलं क्षिपेत्। तदग्र उत्तरदिग्मागस् काष्ठमूलं क्षिपेत्।

शिरः काष्ठमूलं क्षिपेत्। एवं पूर्व दक्षिण पश्चिमोत्तसस्थानेन न्यासे कृते प्रदक्षिणाग्रं भवति। शिरः पादभागकाष्ठयो रेकस्यां
दिश्यग्रं यद् भवति तदैकदिगग्रम्। Ibid.

explaining the comments of Utpala after explaining Işă.
Two holes were made at the ends of the
each of the two shorter beams and the side beams were then fixed into them.
In doing so a
definite order was followed. In the tip (agra) of the head beam was thrown the foot (müla) of the
right side beam;
the latter's top was fixed into the foot of the foot side beam;
the latter's tip was
fitted in the foot of the left side beam;
the latter's tip was joined with the foot of the head side
flank. It was known as Pradakşiņāgra order.

On verses 110-114, 115, 116 - Dr. Raghavan says as under :-
The sixth series taken up by Bhoja in the Kridartha class is the fountain i.e. väri-yantra,
described in some details by Somadeva and dealt with by Bhoja not only here, but also
earlier under palace architecture.
Movment in the Varī yantra is fourfold -
(a) a downward flow from an overhead tank for which a păta-yantra or water fall
machine, is to be used
(b) Samanādikā is for the release of water at a higher level from tanks placed at that
level.
(c) Pātasamaucchraya is a contrivance using bored columns for letting down water from
a height and then taking it up through columns placed aslant and
(d) the last, Ucchraya in which water from a well or in a canal on the ground is sent up
by a device (verses 110-114).
An artificial object which was probably common in Bhoja's time is a wooden elephant
which Bhoja describes twice;
earlier he cited it as an example of various wonderful effects,
that could be achieved through yantras (verses 72-73).
It occurs here again under yantras
based on the principle of sending water upward.
Ucchārya (verse 115), this wooden
elephant drinks water placed in a vessel, any amount of it and neither the intake nor the
water taken in is perceivable on the same Ucchāya principle of circulation of water on the
same level is based the underground conduit which brings water to a tank from a distant
source;
water conduits in general are described earlier also in chapter 18 in connection with
city and residence Bhoja translates Dharāgṛha as shower bower in a garden.

On verses 117-118, Chapter 31, referring to Pravarşaņa as shower, Pranala as pipe,

in palaces for the king's pleasure.
Regarding their construction Bhoja says :-
(1) They are to be in the proximity of big reservoirs.
(2) They should occupy a site with good scenic possibilities.
(3) Pipes have to be prepared to double and treble the height and other requirements of
the fountains;
the pipes should be able to carry water, be free from pores, and smooth inside
(verses 119-120).

order.

winter to the summer solstice)¹ the sacred one, the bright fortnight and auspicious day.

mixed with curd one may adore Soma regularly.
कुबेरं धूपदानेन पूजयेत् सततं नरः।
अदितिं च सुवर्णेन पदौरपि च पूजयेत्।। २४।।
To Kuber by the gift of incense, the person may adore always and to Aditi by gold and
also by lotuses he may adore.
अर्कमन्दारमालाभिर्वृषभं च समर्चयेत्।
अन्येषामपि देवानामर्चनं धूपसाम्प्रतैः (?) ।॥२५॥
To Vrşabha one may adore with Sunflower, Mandāra wreaths and of other gods also the
adoration suits by incense and the like.
सर्वपुष्पफलैश्चैषां कार्यं बुद्धिमता सदा।
इत्येते बलयः सर्वे शान्त्यर्थं परिकल्पिताः ।।२६।।
With the flower and fruits of all kinds, of all these deserves to be done the adoration by
the wise one. All these offerings are meant for the purpose of gratification.

440
Samarangaņa-sūtradhāra
शोधने कर्षणे भूमेः साधने रूपकल्पने।
गृहे प्रवेशने रम्ये तिथिमभ्युदयेषु च (?) ।॥२७॥
In the sweeping and tilling of the land and in polishing and moulding and in the entrance
of the house, (one may take note of) the date as also during the developments.
स्कन्धावारनिवेशेषु पुरग्रामनिवेशने।
देवालयक्षितिपवेश्मनिवेशनेषु
प्रोक्तान् बलीन् प्रवितरेत् प्रयतः सुरेभ्यः ।
प्रारम्भमन्यमपि वास्तुगतं चिकीर्षुः
कुर्वन्निमं विधिमभीप्सितभाजनं स्यात् ।। २८।।
In the establishments of the army camp and in founding down of town, village (and the
city), and in foundations of the temples, the palaces of kings, one may allocate offerings,
the disciplined one, for the gods.
And desirous of other allied foundation laying also,
dealing with Architectural structures, taking to such a norm, one may be a receptacle of the
cherished end.
इति महाराजाधिराजश्रीभोजदेवविरचिते समराङ्गणसूत्रधारापरनाम्नि वास्तुशास्त्रे
बलिदानविधिर्नाम षट्त्रिंशोऽध्यायः ।। ३६ ।।.
